Das Fachwissen bringen wir dir bei. Was man nicht lernen kann, ist dein Wille, mehr aus dir zu machen.

Über den Job:

Als Vertriebsmitarbeiter (m/w/d) telefonierst du mit Inhabern von Handwerksbetrieben, Küchenstudios und Einrichtungshäusern und findest heraus, wo es gerade hakt: Fehlen Kunden, fehlen Mitarbeiter oder laufen die Abläufe nicht rund? Dann prüfst du, ob wir helfen können und ob beide Seiten zusammenpassen.

Jedes Gespräch läuft anders. Das ist Kaltakquise im besten Sinn: Du lernst schnell, wie man Menschen wirklich abholt.

Dein Weg: vom Quereinstieg zu mehr Verantwortung:

1. Ankommen: Du gehst die Schulungen durch, wirst eingearbeitet, lernst die Skripte und hörst zu.

2. Erste Gespräche: Du führst deine ersten eigenen Gespräche und bekommst Call-Reviews mit direktem Feedback dazu.

3. Eigenständig arbeiten: Du arbeitest selbstständig und eigenverantwortlich.

Was dich bei uns erwartet:

  • Klare Struktur: Du hast von Anfang an einen festen Ansprechpartner und einen klaren Fahrplan.

  • Tägliche 1:1-Schulung: Wir analysieren schwierige Gespräche gemeinsam, hören live mit und geben dir direkt Feedback.

  • Teamgefühl trotz Remote: Morgen-Huddle um 7:30 Uhr, Midday-Huddle um 13 Uhr und Roleplays im Team.

  • Transparenz: Du erfährst, was aus deinen Terminen wird und wie sich deine Zahlen entwickeln.

  • Offene Kommunikation: Bei uns kannst du sagen, was dich stört. Wir finden Lösungen.

  • Kein Rädchen im System: Du bist Teil des Teams und kannst wirklich etwas bewirken.

  • Entwicklung: Qualifier oder Teamleiter sind möglich

Das verdienst du:

  • Fixgehalt als sichere Basis: Du startest mit einem festen Gehalt ab 36.000 € brutto im Jahr, je nach Qualifikation ist eine Überzahlung möglich. So kannst du dich voll auf deinen Einstieg konzentrieren.

  • Provision auf deine Ergebnisse: Was du leistest, siehst du auch auf deiner Abrechnung. Wer mehr rausholt, verdient mehr.

  • Mehr als Geld: Du lernst, überzeugend zu sprechen, mit Ablehnung umzugehen und dich selbst zu organisieren. Das bringt dich auch außerhalb des Jobs weiter.

Deine Aufgaben:

  • Du telefonierst mit Entscheidern aus dem Handwerk und der Einrichtungsbranche und führst Bedarfsgespräche.

  • Du vereinbarst Termine für unser Vertriebsteam.

  • Du arbeitest mit klaren Kennzahlen und Zielen und analysierst deine Gespräche selbst.

  • Du nimmst an Trainings, Reviews und Roleplays teil.

Requirements

Das bringst du mit:

  • Lernbereitschaft: Du willst dich verbessern und bist bereit, dafür mehr zu geben als nötig.

  • Standhaftigkeit: Ein Nein bringt dich nicht aus dem Konzept. Du bleibst offen für das nächste gute Gespräch.

  • Zielorientierung: Du magst Ziele, Zahlen und Wettbewerb und willst dich daran messen.

  • Ehrlichkeit und Kommunikation: Du sagst offen, was los ist, und nimmst Feedback an, auch wenn es direkt ist.

  • Commitment: Wenn du dich für etwas entscheidest, ziehst du es durch.

  • Reisebereitschaft: Du kommst 3- bis 4-mal im Jahr für jeweils 1 Woche zum Bootcamp nach Wörgl.

  • Rahmen: Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse, ruhiger Arbeitsplatz zu Hause mit stabilem Internet, Vollzeit von Montag bis Freitag.

Keine Vertriebserfahrung? Kein Problem! Wir bringen dir alles bei, was du brauchst.

jobs.title: Recruiter
jobs.excerpt: Maybe you call yourself a Recruiter, a Talent Scout, a Sourcing Specialist, a People Finder… or maybe you just call yourself Jo.
jobs.description:
Maybe you call yourself a Recruiter, a Talent Scout, a Sourcing Specialist, a People Finder… or maybe you just call yourself Jo.

Whatever you call yourself: you'll help us find and connect with the people we need as we grow, from data engineers and consultants to the people who keep our business running.

What you get

  • A salary of €48,600–€61,560 gross per year, depending on your experience and living in the Netherlands. We use salary zones, so the range may be lower elsewhere in Europe. We’ll share the exact range for your country before your first interview.

  • €5,000 a year for your own growth, with a real say in how you spend it.

  • 25 vacation days + the option to buy up to 10 more + local public holidays + the option of a sabbatical up to 4 months.

  • Two trips abroad a year with the whole team + occasional drinks and team outings.

  • €500 home-office budget and a great laptop.

  • A well-earned "Hey, well done Buddy!" now and then.

  • Remote-first, anywhere in the EU/EEA

About us

All Your BI is a remote-first data agency based in Rotterdam. Since 2019, we've grown from a boutique consultancy into an international data team of more than 60 data heroes spread across Europe. We deliver managed BI services for logistics and industrial companies, helping reduce data waste and move businesses forward. We live for the WOW moment, that sparkle in users' eyes when they gain new insights and discover opportunities.

What the job looks like

Design your sourcing strategy: Join intake meetings with hiring teams to understand what they need and the profiles we're looking for. Turn that into a sourcing plan, deciding where to find people, which channels to use and what approaches to try. You'll have the opportunity to take ownership of your searches, experiment and learn what works.

Find and engage great people: Put your strategy into action. Research potential candidates through LinkedIn, GitHub, professional communities and your own network. Reach out, introduce them to AYBI and build relationships with people who could be a great fit.

Keep recruitment moving: Coordinate interviews, follow up with candidates and manage pipelines. Keep candidate records and our hiring tracker up to date so everyone knows where things stand and nothing falls through the cracks.

Create a great candidate experience: Be responsive, communicate openly and give honest feedback. No ghosting.

Build our employer brand: Help shape how AYBI shows up in the recruitment market. We want people to know who we are and what makes working here different, and you'll have a hand in making that happen.

Work together: Work closely with the Talent Acquisition Partner, freelance recruiters, People Partners and hiring Captains. Share what you're seeing in the market and bring ideas to improve how we attract and recruit people.

We're self-managed, so you'll have plenty of freedom to organise your work and make decisions. You won't always get a perfect brief or a step-by-step manual. We expect you to figure things out, ask questions, take initiative and challenge the way things are done. You'll also have plenty of room to develop your recruitment skills, learn from the people around you and gradually take on more responsibility.

Requirements

What you bring

Attitude and energy: Curiosity, initiative and a genuine interest in people. You enjoy connecting with others and care about doing a good job.

Recruitment and sourcing experience: Around 1–3 years in agency or in-house recruitment, with practical, hands-on experience sourcing candidates. You know how to find and approach people, build candidate pipelines and start meaningful conversations. You're ready to take more ownership of your searches and develop your skills in working with hiring teams and designing sourcing strategies.

Tech curiosity: You're interested in data and software engineering and enjoy learning what makes a great technical candidate. You don't need to be a developer or have recruited every type of technical profile before.

Creativity and communication: You're a good communicator with an eye for engaging content. You enjoy coming up with ideas, telling stories and finding ways to get people's attention. Experience with social media or employer branding is a bonus.

Ownership and judgment: You turn a thin brief into a plan, take responsibility for your searches and bring ideas and recommendations rather than just questions. You know when to make a call and when to ask for input, and you do what you say you'll do.

Communication and tools: You're curious about how AI and recruitment tools can improve your work, and you use them thoughtfully.

Language and location: Fluent English, both written and spoken. Dutch is a bonus, not a requirement. You're based somewhere in the EU/EEA, with good overlap with Dutch working hours.

Nice to have: Experience recruiting for Microsoft, data or cloud-related roles, or previous involvement in employer branding.

We're a growing team across Europe, and we hire to widen that mix, not narrow it. What matters is what you can do and the perspective you bring, not your age, gender, ethnicity, orientation, disability, background or where you studied. If the role excites you and you bring most of it, apply: the people who add the most rarely tick every box.

Highlights

Help us find great people across Europe as our next Recruiter. Own your sourcing strategy, build relationships and grow your recruitment skills in a remote-first team.

jobs.description:
Senior Staff Attorney, Pregnancy & Postpartum Workplace Rights

WorkLife Law

Classification: Level 4 / Class 2502 (Center Senior Associate) / Exempt / Full-Time / Benefited / Non-represented

Work Arrangement: Fully Remote

Anticipated hiring range: $105,000 - $130,000 (commensurate with qualifications, location and experience)

Term: One-year term, with the initial appointment and subsequent renewal contingent upon the continuation of grant funding. (WorkLife Law has been awarded a grant that runs through December 2029 that will cover all costs associated with this position.)

WorkLife Law seeks an experienced attorney to join our team as a Senior Staff Attorney. The Senior Staff Attorney will spend most of their time on Expecting Change: Supporting Pregnant and Postpartum Workers, a three-year project funded by WorkLife Law’s recent award from the Workplace Innovation Now (WIN) Challenge. The Senior Staff Attorney will play a key role on the project team and will be responsible for training healthcare providers on their patients’ workplace rights during pregnancy and the postpartum period as well as directly assisting workers through WorkLife Law’s free legal helpline. As time permits, they will also contribute to WorkLife Law’s broader advocacy.

ABOUT WORKLIFE LAW

WorkLife Law is a national advocacy and research organization that advances gender and racial equity by strengthening legal rights for pregnant people and family caregivers. Our work seeks to ensure all people have the freedom to build and maintain economic security through employment and educational opportunities, without having to sacrifice their health or their loved ones’ care. As a center of the University of California College of the Law, San Francisco, WorkLife Law provides direct assistance to workers and students in need and addresses structural inequality by changing public policy at the state and national levels.

Related to this position, WorkLife Law has been a national leader in implementing the Pregnant Workers Fairness Act (PWFA) since its enactment in 2023. WorkLife Law helped shape the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission’s (EEOC’s) PWFA regulations and co-authored the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists’ (ACOG’s) clinical guidance on the new law. Institutions ranging from teaching hospitals to small community clinics regularly invite WorkLife Law to train their clinicians, and we trained nearly 1,600 healthcare providers in 2025 alone. In 2026, WorkLife Law’s helpline experienced the highest call volume in its nearly 25-year history. Nine out of ten workers who receive support through our free helpline get the accommodations and leave they are seeking without having to file a legal claim.

THE ROLE AND RESPONSIBILITIES

The Senior Staff Attorney’s time will be spent primarily advancing our new initiative, Expecting Change: Supporting Pregnant and Postpartum Workers. In October 2026, WorkLife Law was selected as one of 18 awardees of the WIN Challenge, chosen from nearly 900 applicants, to promote women’s economic security. The WIN Challenge is led by Aspen Digital, a program of the Aspen Institute, and supported by Pivotal, a group of social impact organizations founded by Melinda French Gates. The three-year, $2.5 million grant funds our Expecting Change initiative and this position.

Healthcare providers are the gatekeepers to pregnancy accommodations and leave, yet the vast majority receive no training on their patients’ workplace rights. Expecting Change will change this by training 10,000 women’s healthcare providers over three years through medical schools, hospitals, clinics, and professional conferences. Our initiative will equip healthcare providers to serve as key messengers in the community about legal rights, giving them practical tools to help their patients stay healthy and employed. The project will also double the capacity of WorkLife Law’s free legal helpline, so that more workers get one-on-one help when facing workplace challenges related to pregnancy, and more employers get clear direction on what the law requires of them. The project’s goal is to make pregnancy-related accommodation routine rather than exceptional.

The Senior Staff Attorney will be a key member of our Expecting Change team, playing central roles in both core aspects of the program by training healthcare providers on their patients’ workplace rights and directly assisting workers through WorkLife Law’s free legal helpline. Beginning in fall 2027, the Senior Staff Attorney will also supervise and mentor a Staff Attorney who will join the project to further expand our capacity to train providers and support helpline callers. The Senior Staff Attorney will report to Co-Director Liz Morris and will work closely with Co-Director Jessica Lee and the rest of the WorkLife Law team, including a Program Manager who will provide logistical and administrative support for Expecting Change.

As time permits, the Senior Staff Attorney will contribute to WorkLife Law’s broader work, including amicus briefs, technical support for litigators, policy advocacy, and know-your-rights resources for pregnant and postpartum workers and family caregivers.

We are looking for an experienced legal advocate who is equally adept at making formal presentations to medical audiences and supporting workers in crisis: someone who can earn the trust of clinicians and influence how they support their patients, who listens with empathy and works sensitively with people facing some of the most stressful moments of their lives, and who can serve as a national voice on these issues.

Typical duties and responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

Healthcare Provider Trainings

  • Deliver engaging, practical trainings to women’s healthcare providers, including physicians, midwives, nurses, residents, mental health professionals, lactation consultants, doulas, and community health workers on pregnant, postpartum, and lactating patients’ workplace rights and how providers can help patients get the accommodations and leave they need. Trainings will typically be virtual although some in-person events are likely.
  • Adapt WorkLife Law’s existing curriculum for different audiences and for the laws of the state where each training takes place, help refine it based on participant evaluations, and keep it current as the law develops.

Direct Assistance to Workers

  • Alongside WorkLife Law’s other attorneys, provide direct assistance to workers on WorkLife Law’s free helpline with compassion, resourcefulness, cultural competency, legal expertise, and clarity. The helpline is a “warm line” where workers from across the country leave messages and our attorneys respond within two business days.
  • Analyze callers’ situations by listening closely, reviewing documents, and applying relevant laws. Formulate a strategy for serving each caller and engage callers throughout the process. Depending on the needs of the individual caller, services will range from answering questions about legal rights and providing know-your-rights materials to writing letters to employers, drafting agency complaints, negotiating settlements, and providing ongoing support over many months.
  • Carefully manage helpline call records, collect demographic and impact data, and seek ways to inform our education, direct service, and advocacy work based on learnings from helpline experiences.

Healthcare Provider Outreach and Relationship-Building

  • Build relationships with healthcare providers and institutions to generate new training opportunities, including by connecting with attendees at presentations. Help prioritize high-impact opportunities, such as major teaching institutions, national conferences, and locations where healthcare providers are least familiar with these protections and/or where are caring for underserved patients.
  • Help Co-Director Morris build WorkLife Law’s Healthcare Provider Advisory Committee and leverage members to support the work of the project.

Resource Creation

  • Create and update practical materials for workers, healthcare providers, and employers, including documents explaining the law for workers; documents explaining employer obligations for use by workers when negotiating with their employers; and tools for healthcare providers and their patients, such as work-note templates, exam room posters, and patient handouts. Resource creation includes researching and fact checking to ensure materials remain up to date, seeking and incorporating feedback from stakeholders to ensure the materials meet their needs, and translating complicated legal ideas into accessible language that is appropriate for the audience at hand.
  • Draft clinical best-practice articles for scholarly journals.

Policy Advocacy: WorkLife Law’s policy advocacy is grounded in what we hear every day from helpline callers. Review helpline trends through that lens, regularly update the WorkLife Law team, and help identify policy solutions to ensure that the experiences of workers and healthcare providers inform WorkLife Law’s policy advocacy and research. Identify helpline callers interested in sharing their experiences to create policy and narrative change.

Supervision: Help recruit and onboard a Staff Attorney who will join the project in fall 2027, then supervise and mentor them as they train healthcare providers and serve helpline callers. Supervise law students as capacity allows.

Project Tracking and Grant Reporting: Working with the Expecting Change Program Manager, track training and helpline metrics and assist with grant reporting.

Broader WorkLife Law Efforts: As time permits, contribute to WorkLife Law’s other work that strengthens and promotes access to legal protections for workers and students who are pregnant and caregiving. This may include drafting amicus briefs in key cases, providing technical assistance to litigators in WorkLife Law’s Attorney Network, educating community-based advocates about legal protections, and/or engaging in policy advocacy.

REQUIREMENTS

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

Education and Experience

  • J.D. degree
  • Admission to practice law in any U.S. state
  • Minimum 5 years of relevant legal experience, we welcome more experienced candidates
  • Experience providing direct services to people in crisis in a culturally competent manner
  • Experience presenting to or training professional audiences
  • Experience supervising attorneys, law students, or other staff is preferred
  • Professional experience in employment law
  • Medical-legal partnership or other healthcare-related experience is a plus

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Familiarity with the PWFA, PUMP Act, and paid family and medical leave programs is strongly preferred, along with knowledge of related employment laws such as Title VII, the ADA, and the FMLA, and their state-law equivalents
  • Working knowledge of the physical and mental health needs of pregnant, postpartum, and lactating workers is strongly preferred
  • Ability to build and maintain trust-based relationships and networks with key allies and stakeholders, and in particular to meaningfully connect with healthcare providers to influence how they support patients
  • Adept at making engaging public presentations and at thoughtfully translating complex legal concepts into accessible language for audiences of varying personal and professional backgrounds
  • Superior research and writing skills, with the ability to write for legal, technical, and lay audiences; proficiency with Lexis and/or Westlaw
  • Ability to speak with people in crisis with compassion and cultural sensitivity; experience working with non-English speakers preferred
  • Keen sense of judgment and tact, including in navigating sensitive dynamics with partners, government officials, and employers
  • Self-starter who can manage projects with minimal supervision, with the ability to both develop a vision and execute on the details
  • Adaptable and resourceful, with an eagerness to problem-solve and the nimbleness to shift between tasks as needs evolve
  • Commitment to workers’ rights, gender equity, language access, and reproductive and racial justice, and to the other goals and values of WorkLife Law
  • Desire to work in a group that prioritizes open communication, work-life balance, and positive relationships
  • Willingness to travel occasionally (approximately two to four trips per year)
  • Fluency in Spanish is a very strong plus

The skills listed above are comprehensive, and we understand that there are great candidates who possess only a subset of those skills, or who have other important skills. If you match some of these skills, please do not hesitate to apply.

BENEFITS

Health and Welfare Benefits

  • Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance coverage
  • Flexible Spending Accounts for transportation-related, healthcare and dependent care expenses
  • Employee Assistance Program

For Your Financial Future

  • Life Insurance, Disability Insurance, and Legal Insurance
  • University of California Retirement Plan (a defined benefit plan)
  • Deferred Compensation Plans/Pre-tax Retirement Savings Programs

For Your Work/Life Balance

  • Fifteen paid holidays per year
  • Generous vacation and sick leave
  • Commuter Benefits Program

THE HIRING PROCESS

We aim to be transparent and efficient in our hiring process. All applications are reviewed by members of WorkLife Law’s team. Application review will begin December 1, 2026.

Interested candidates should submit the following materials with their application:

  • Resume
  • Detailed cover letter: Your cover letter should explain why you would like to work for WorkLife Law on our Expecting Change initiative. Highlight relevant experience you have, particularly related to employment law, advocacy on behalf of pregnant/postpartum workers, training or presenting to professional audiences (especially healthcare providers), and providing direct services (whether legal or otherwise).

Later stage candidates will be asked for a list of three professional references and a writing sample.

This hiring process will include two video interview rounds and a skills assessment. In each interview, you will be asked to provide examples of these skills and experiences or explain how you would draw on your experiences to handle a scenario commonly found at WorkLife Law.

WorkLife Law is committed to building a diverse and inclusive team. We encourage applications from members of underrepresented communities and are eager to provide disability accommodations, when needed.

Please note: This position has been designated as “sensitive” and requires a pre-employment background check.

Federal law requires employers to provide reasonable accommodation to qualified individuals with disabilities. Please contact Human Resources if you require a reasonable accommodation to apply for a job. Examples of reasonable accommodation include making a change to the application process, providing documents in an alternate format, using a sign language interpreter, or using specialized equipment

WHAT TO EXPECT

Applicants who meet the position requirements will be competitively evaluated to identify the individuals whose breadth and depth of experience and education most closely relate to the stated requirements and the needs of the College. Not all applicants will be contacted for an interview.

UC Law San Francisco is an Equal Opportunity Employer. UC Law San Francisco strives to provide a diverse and inclusive educational environment that fosters cultural awareness, mutual understanding and respect. UC Law San Francisco College of the Law is interested in candidates who will contribute to diversity and equal opportunity in higher education through their teaching. Qualified women and members of underrepresented minority groups are strongly encouraged to apply

jobs.title: Freelance AI Consultant Dierenwelzijn
jobs.excerpt: 📋 Taken en verantwoordelijkheden Binnen het domein dierenwelzijn is er behoefte aan een medior AI Consultant die instaat voor de technische ontwikkeling, het testen en de optimalisatie van AI-oplossingen in een case managementsysteem voor inspectiedossiers.
jobs.description:
📋 Taken en verantwoordelijkheden

Binnen het domein dierenwelzijn is er behoefte aan een medior AI Consultant die instaat voor de technische ontwikkeling, het testen en de optimalisatie van AI-oplossingen in een case managementsysteem voor inspectiedossiers.

Er wordt onderzocht hoe AI kan worden geïntegreerd om medewerkers te ondersteunen bij de behandeling en opvolging van dossiers. Een eerste concrete use case is het automatisch analyseren en classificeren van binnenkomende meldingen. Daarbij kan gebruik worden gemaakt van beslissingsbomen, historische dossiers en beschikbare contextinformatie. Het doel is om meldingen sneller en consistenter te beoordelen en medewerkers gericht te ondersteunen bij de verdere behandeling van dossiers.

Daarnaast worden bijkomende mogelijkheden voor AI onderzocht en gerealiseerd. Die kunnen onder meer gericht zijn op het vereenvoudigen van administratieve en repetitieve taken, het ontsluiten van relevante informatie uit dossiers en het ondersteunen van medewerkers bij dossierbehandeling en besluitvorming.

De medior AI Consultant werkt samen met een senior AI Consultant in een technisch AI-team. De senior consultant bepaalt mee de technische richting, architectuur en kwaliteitskaders. De medior consultant focust vooral op praktische ontwikkeling, prototyping, experimenten, testing en het iteratief verbeteren van AI-componenten.

De opdracht is nadrukkelijk ontwikkelingsgericht en omvat meer dan een analyserende of adviserende rol.

De werkzaamheden omvatten onder meer:

  • Meewerken aan de analyse van data, documenten, historische dossiers en businessregels voor AI-use-cases.
  • Ontwikkelen van prototypes en proof-of-concepts.
  • Programmeren en configureren van AI-componenten.
  • Experimenteren met verschillende modellen, prompts, classificatiemethodes en andere AI-technieken.
  • Meewerken aan de oplossing voor automatische analyse, classificatie en triage van meldingen.
  • Voorbereiden, verwerken en analyseren van data voor AI-toepassingen.
  • Implementeren van oplossingen op basis van machine learning, NLP en generatieve AI/LLM's.
  • Testen uitvoeren met representatieve dossiers en praktijksituaties.
  • De kwaliteit en betrouwbaarheid van verschillende oplossingsrichtingen meten en vergelijken.
  • Foutieve of onvoldoende betrouwbare resultaten analyseren en de oplossing technisch bijsturen.
  • Prompts, modellen, businessregels en andere AI-componenten optimaliseren.
  • Koppelingen tussen AI-componenten en het case managementsysteem mee uitwerken en testen.
  • Code, modellen, databronnen, configuraties en testresultaten technisch documenteren.
  • Samenwerken met een senior AI Consultant, bestaande ontwikkelaars, technische partners en de business.
  • Onder begeleiding van de senior consultant onderdelen van AI-oplossingen zelfstandig uitwerken van prototype tot bruikbare technische component.

📝 Jouw profiel

  • Je hebt ervaring als AI Consultant op mediorniveau en neemt een praktische ontwikkelrol op.
  • Je hebt ervaring met case managementsystemen.
  • Je beschikt over programmeerkennis in Python. Ervaring met R of Java is eveneens relevant voor het ontwikkelen van AI-toepassingen.
  • Je hebt ervaring binnen de publieke sector of in andere complexe organisaties.
  • Je kent cloudplatforms zoals AWS, Azure of Google Cloud voor het schalen van AI-oplossingen.
  • Je hebt kennis van verschillende machine learning-technieken.

⚠️ Deze functie wordt aangeboden als een deeltijdse freelance rol (50%).

jobs.title: Cloud & Backend Software Engineer
jobs.excerpt: Overview CLOUD & BACKEND SOFTWARE ENGINEER (ERDC AI-DRIVEN ENGINEERING QA/QC): Bowhead is seeking a Cloud & Backend Software Engineer to support the development of an AI-driven Engineering Quality Assurance / Quality Control (QA/QC) capability for the Engineering Research and Development Center (ERDC).
jobs.description:
Overview

CLOUD & BACKEND SOFTWARE ENGINEER (ERDC AI-DRIVEN ENGINEERING QA/QC):

Bowhead is seeking a Cloud & Backend Software Engineer to support the development of an AI-driven Engineering Quality Assurance / Quality Control (QA/QC) capability for the Engineering Research and Development Center (ERDC). Support for this new three-year research effort will consist of developing an AI-enabled platform to automate engineering design reviews across drawings, specifications, calculations, and multiple engineering disciplines. The long-term goal of the project is to move beyond traditional compliance checks by incorporating computational modeling, uncertainty, reliability, and performance-based assessments to support engineering decision-making.

Responsibilities

  • Design, develop, and maintain Python-based APIs and microservices using FastAPI and/or Flask.
  • Design, deploy, and manage secure, reliable, and scalable cloud-based applications and services.
  • Automate application deployment, testing, and integration using CI/CD pipelines.
  • Containerize and orchestrate services using Docker and Kubernetes.
  • Provision and manage cloud infrastructure using Infrastructure as Code (IaC) principles.
  • Take ownership of technical tasks, think independently, contribute to architectural decisions, and see development efforts through from concept to implementation.
  • Work with and leverage AI technologies to support automated engineering design review workflows.

Qualifications

• BS degree in Computer Science or relevant field PLUS five (5+) years of relevant software development experience
• Strong Python programming skills, including experience with FastAPI and/or Flask for developing APIs and microservices.
• Experience automating application deployment, testing, and integration via CI/CD pipelines.
• Ability to develop secure, reliable, and scalable cloud-based architectures.
• Familiarity with containerization and orchestration tools, including Docker and Kubernetes.
• Ability to take ownership of technical tasks, think independently, and contribute to architectural decisions.
• Willingness to learn how to work with and leverage AI technologies (prior AI or machine learning experience is not required).
• Preferred: Experience designing, deploying, and managing cloud-based applications and services within Microsoft Azure (can be taught to individuals with a strong development background).
• Preferred: Experience with Terraform for provisioning and managing cloud infrastructure (can be taught).
• Preferred: Experience with Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) (can be taught).

Physical Demands:

  • Must be able to lift 25 pounds
  • Must be able to stand and walk for prolonged amounts of time
  • Must be able to twist, bend, and squat periodically

The pay scale for this position is between $110,000 - $130,000.

Please note that the salary information is a general guideline only. Bowhead considers factors such as (but not limited to) scope and responsibilities of the position, candidate’s work experience, education/training, key skills, internal peer equity, as well as, market and business considerations when extending an offer.

SECURITY CLEARANCE REQUIRED: Must be able to obtain a security clearance at the Secret level. US Citizenship is a requirement for Secret clearance at this location.

jobs.title: Technical Support Engineer
jobs.excerpt: Who We Are: We’re Aspire and FieldRoutes, the leading SaaS providers for the landscaping, commercial cleaning, pest control and lawn care industries and proud members of the ServiceTitan family since 2021.
jobs.description:
Who We Are:

We’re Aspire and FieldRoutes, the leading SaaS providers for the landscaping, commercial cleaning, pest control and lawn care industries and proud members of the ServiceTitan family since 2021. Our cloud-based business management systems automate all aspects of field service operations for enterprise and small to medium-sized businesses enabling our clients to accelerate growth, streamline operations, increase customer retention, and maximize revenue. Trusted by thousands of premier field services leaders in the U.S. and Canada, our solutions empower our clients to make better business decisions for their companies. Our partnership with ServiceTitan has enabled us to continue scaling our platforms and customer base while maintaining our collaborative, tight-knit culture.

TA’s standard paragraph, left as is.

What We’re Looking For:

As a Technical Support Engineer (TSE), you’ll be Tier 2 support for Aspire and FieldRoutes. When a client problem is more than our Tier 1 team can solve, the case is transferred to you, and it’s yours until it’s resolved. You find the cause, fix the data or get the bug to our developers, and keep the client informed the whole way.

We use AI tools for the first pass on cases. They pull a case together, look for known bugs and similar past cases, search our knowledge base, and help draft SQL. You check what they find before anything reaches a client, and you take on the problems they can’t solve.

We want someone who likes figuring out why software breaks and can explain it in plain language. This is a mid-level role with a path to Senior Technical Support Engineer, reporting to the Manager of Technical Support Engineering.

What You’ll Do:

Own your cases

  • Take ownership of cases transferred from Tier 1, work them in order of client impact, and see each one through to resolution, including while a fix is with development.
  • Find the root cause by reproducing the issue and digging into the client’s data with SQL and our application logs.
  • Decide whether an issue is a bug, a data problem, or a how-to question, and route it to the right place.
  • Write Jira bug reports a developer can act on without a follow-up call, with clear steps, expected and actual results, and the data involved.
  • Fix bad data with careful SQL scripts and log every correction. Validate and load client data imports.
  • Build and check custom FieldRoutes layouts in HTML.
  • Keep clients updated by email and phone in plain language, and confirm a fix is live before you tell them it’s done.

Use AI, and check it

  • Use our AI assistants for first-pass research, then check what they report against the client’s actual data. You’re accountable for what goes to a client, and anything our bots post is labeled as automated.
  • When an assistant gets something wrong, correct it so the next answer is right. Write the knowledge base articles and runbooks that your teammates and our AI tools both rely on.
  • Help improve the team’s scripts and AI skills, which live in GitHub. You don’t need to be a developer, but you should be willing to read and edit a script or a prompt.

Beyond your own queue

  • Coach Tier 1 when a case could have been solved at their level, and help write the SOPs and training that let them solve more on first contact.
  • Help rank the bugs that hurt clients most so development fixes the right ones first.
  • Own a few improvement projects each quarter. Our team runs on EOS, so you’ll hear these called Rocks.

How We Measure Success:

Each quarter we look at the cases you solved and how long they took, your client satisfaction (CSAT) scores, the Rocks you finished, and what you added to the team’s tools and knowledge base.

What You’ll Need:

  • 2+ years in technical support, application support, or another client-facing technical role, ideally at a B2B software company
  • SQL you’ve used on real data, including joins, grouping, and subqueries, and enough comfort to read a stored procedure and follow what it does (Aspire runs on SQL Server, FieldRoutes on MySQL)
  • Regular use of AI tools such as Claude, ChatGPT, or Copilot in your day-to-day work, with the habit of checking their answers and good judgment about what client data goes into them
  • Clear writing: you can explain a technical cause to a client in a few sentences and write a bug report a developer can follow
  • Experience with a case management system such as Salesforce or Zendesk, and with Jira or a similar issue tracker
  • Comfort switching between two products built on different technology in the same day

Be Human With Us:
Being human isn’t about checking every box on a list. It’s about the experiences we have, people we meet, and the perspectives we share. So, if you have the skills but are hesitant to apply because of your background, apply anyway. We need amazing people like you to help us challenge the conventional and think differently about the problems that we’re solving. We’re in this together. Come be human, with us.


Use of AI Technology:

We use technology, including automated and AI-assisted tools, to support certain aspects of our recruitment process. These tools are designed to improve efficiency and enhance the candidate experience. AI tools are not used to make hiring decisions; all hiring decisions are made by our hiring teams.


What We Offer:

When you join our team, you’re not just accepting a job. You’re making a career move. Here’s how we’ll support you in doing some of the most impactful work of your career:

  • Flextime, recognition, and support for autonomous work: Flexible time off with ample learning and development opportunities to continue growing your career. We offer a comprehensive onboarding program, leadership training for Titans at all levels, and other programs and events. Great work is rewarded through Bonusly, peer-nominated awards, and more.
  • Holistic health and wellness benefits: Company-paid medical, dental, and vision (with 100% employer paid options and 90% coverage for dependents), FSA and HSA, 401k match, and telehealth options including memberships to One Medical.
  • Support for Titans at all stages of life: Parental leave and support, up to $20k in fertility services (i.e. IUI and IVF), surrogacy, and adoption reimbursement, on demand maternity support through Maven Maternity, free breast milk shipping through Maven Milk, pet insurance, legal advisory services, financial planning tools, and more.

At ServiceTitan, we celebrate individuality and uniqueness. We believe that the convergence of fresh perspectives and experiences from all walks of life is what makes our product and culture so great. We strongly encourage people from underrepresented groups to apply. We do not discriminate against employees based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, gender identity or expression, age, disability, pregnancy (including childbirth, breastfeeding, or related medical condition), genetic information, protected military or veteran status, sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state or local laws.

ServiceTitan is committed to fair and equitable compensation for all of our employees. We thoughtfully consider a wide range of factors when determining individual compensation, which may change over time. We comply with all applicable minimum wage laws. For candidates in the United States, the good faith salary ranges estimate for this role isZone 1: $70,500 USD - $105,700 USD Applicable for: CA, CT, DC, MD, MA, NJ, NY, VA, and WAZone 2: $65,800 USD - $98,800 USD Applicable for: All other US locations.International Compensation for candidates residing outside the United States will vary by location and will be discussed during the hiring process. Actual compensation within a range is determined by factors including relevant experience, skill set, qualifications, and performance. In addition to base salary, our total compensation package includes an annual bonus, equity, and a holistic suite of benefits.

jobs.title: Growth and Business Enablement Lead
jobs.excerpt: Leidos has an exciting opportunity within the Corporate Information Security (CIS) Mission Cybersecurity (MC) organization for a Growth and Business Enablement Lead.
jobs.description:
Leidos has an exciting opportunity within the Corporate Information Security (CIS) Mission Cybersecurity (MC) organization for a Growth and Business Enablement Lead. This senior individual contributor will serve as the primary integration point between Mission Cybersecurity and Leidos Sector Growth organizations, helping turn new business opportunities into secure, executable missions.

Location: This position is able to work onsite in our Reston, VA headquarters or fully remote from any U.S. based location.


Citizenship: U.S. Citizenship is required.


Mission Cybersecurity provides the Information Assurance and secure IT capabilities that enable Leidos programs to execute sensitive missions. Our team works across the enterprise to solve complex business challenges, remove barriers to execution, and help our programs succeed. Cybersecurity is most effective when it enables the mission.

The Growth and Business Enablement Lead will serve as a strategic partner to Leidos Sector Growth, Capture, Finance, and Program leadership, helping shape competitive, cost-effective, and executable solutions for new business opportunities. Working across Mission Cybersecurity, this individual will identify opportunities to leverage existing capabilities, reusable solutions, and proven performance to strengthen proposals, improve cost competitiveness, and differentiate Leidos in the marketplace. The role requires the ability to look beyond stated requirements, challenge assumptions, develop creative alternatives, and help capture teams balance mission objectives, security requirements, cost, schedule, and execution risk. This is an opportunity to influence how Leidos pursues and executes new business across the enterprise, connecting growth opportunities with the capabilities, expertise, and innovative solutions of Mission Cybersecurity.

In this role, you will also maintain an enterprise view of MC growth demand across Leidos, identifying common requirements, emerging capability needs, long-lead dependencies, and risks that could affect future program execution. Following an award, the Growth and Business Enablement Lead will coordinate MC's transition from proposal to execution, ensuring operational teams are positioned to successfully deliver the commitments made during capture.

Success requires someone who enjoys bringing people together to solve difficult problems. The ideal candidate is proactive, comfortable operating across organizational boundaries, and skilled at influencing outcomes without direct authority. They can bring structure to ambiguity and persistently drive actions to closure. They will engage early, solve problems collaboratively, and make Mission Cybersecurity a competitive advantage for Leidos.

You won't be expected to have every answer yourself. Your job is to bring the right people together, ask the right questions, anticipate what comes next, and make sure critical activities get done. The work is highly collaborative, and the problems are rarely identical.

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Serve as Mission Cybersecurity's primary integration point with Leidos Sector Growth and capture organizations, providing a consistent and responsive approach to supporting new business opportunities across the enterprise.
  • Engage early in strategic pursuits to help Sector Growth and Capture teams shape solutions, acquisition approaches, security requirements, and competitive discriminators by leveraging Mission Cybersecurity expertise, existing capabilities, reusable solutions, and past performance to strengthen proposals, improve Leidos' competitive position, and reduce downstream execution risk.
  • Proactively engage Sector Growth and Capture organizations across the enterprise to identify opportunities where MC capabilities can improve proposed solutions, strengthen competitive positioning, and reduce execution risk. Maintain an integrated view of the MC growth pipeline to identify emerging demand, opportunities for reuse, and strategic actions that improve business outcomes.
  • Partner with capture teams and MC technical experts to evaluate proposed mission solutions, challenge assumptions, identify alternative approaches, and develop secure, cost-effective, and executable solutions that meet customer requirements while improving Leidos' competitive position.
  • Develop and coordinate MC Basis of Estimates (BOEs) for growth opportunities using established MC estimating tools and methodologies, including Information Assurance and Secure IT labor, infrastructure, connectivity, and other applicable MC costs.
  • Partner with capture managers to identify secure facilities, infrastructure, connectivity, capacity, and other dependencies required to execute proposed work.
  • Establish and mature MC's growth portfolio management process, including the governance, measures, operating rhythms, and reporting necessary to provide leadership with an enterprise view of growth demand.
  • Develop requirements for dashboards and supporting tools that enable MC to measure and manage proposal activity, transition status, upcoming capacity needs, common capability requirements, and risks requiring leadership attention.
  • Consolidate requirements from multiple Sector Growth organizations into a prioritized enterprise view, translating business demand into actionable requirements for MC.
  • Identify trends across the growth pipeline that indicate emerging capability, infrastructure, facility, staffing, connectivity, and capacity needs. Proactively develop requirements and business cases to address them before they constrain business execution.
  • Own MC coordination of the post-award transition from proposal through successful handoff to MC Operations, ensuring commitments made during capture are understood, planned, tracked, and driven to closure.
  • Coordinate long-lead activities such as government circuit orders and moves, secure network connectivity, infrastructure readiness, workstation and capacity planning, and other dependencies that could affect program start-up schedules.
  • Participate as the MC representative on teams responsible for establishing new secure spaces, including facility planning, build-out, accreditation, connectivity, and transition activities.
  • Support building moves and other facility changes driven by business growth, ensuring MC requirements and dependencies are incorporated early enough to support the business schedule.
  • Establish clear owners, milestones, dependencies, risks, and escalation paths for complex cross-functional activities and proactively follow actions through completion.
  • Build productive relationships with Sector Growth executives, capture managers, program leaders, MC Operations, Corporate Security, facilities organizations, government stakeholders, subcontractors, and other partners necessary to deliver business outcomes.
  • Influence stakeholders across organizational boundaries and drive timely decisions and actions without direct management authority.
  • Regularly brief MC leadership on the enterprise growth portfolio, upcoming demand, significant transitions, common capability needs, emerging risks, and decisions requiring leadership attention.
  • Capture lessons learned from proposals and transitions and continuously improve MC's processes, estimating approaches, engagement model, and ability to support Leidos growth.
  • Foster a collaborative, mission-focused culture where MC is viewed as a trusted business partner that helps Leidos securely make the business opportunity happen.

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree with 8–12 years of relevant experience, or an equivalent combination of education, certifications, training, and relevant professional experience.
  • Demonstrated ability to evaluate business or technical challenges, develop alternative approaches, and influence stakeholders toward solutions that improve cost, schedule, risk, or operational outcomes.
  • Proven ability to move beyond stated requirements to understand underlying business objectives, challenge assumptions constructively, and identify opportunities to improve proposed solutions.
  • Ability to operate as a trusted advisor to business and technical stakeholders, combining sound judgment, creativity, and collaboration to solve complex problems and drive results.
  • Proven ability to influence without direct authority and build consensus among stakeholders with differing priorities, responsibilities, and objectives.
  • Demonstrated ability to proactively coordinate people and organizations, establish clear actions and deadlines, follow up persistently, identify barriers, and drive activities through successful completion.
  • Strong project and program management skills with experience managing multiple concurrent efforts with cross-functional components, dependencies, schedules, risks, and priorities.
  • Ability to take ambiguous or complex business needs and translate them into structured requirements, processes, actions, and measurable outcomes.
  • Strong interpersonal skills and demonstrated ability to establish trusted relationships with technical teams, operational organizations, business leaders, and senior stakeholders.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate complex technical or operational topics to audiences with varying levels of expertise.
  • Demonstrated ability to identify risks and dependencies early, develop mitigation approaches, and appropriately escalate issues requiring leadership action.
  • Strong business acumen and demonstrated ability to evaluate tradeoffs among cost, schedule, technical requirements, security risk, and mission objectives to recommend practical solutions that improve business competitiveness and execution success.
  • Self-starter who demonstrates initiative, persistence, sound judgment, creativity, and personal accountability for results.
  • Ability to understand technical concepts sufficiently to challenge assumptions, identify potential gaps and risks, and engage the appropriate subject matter experts when deeper expertise is required.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Government security clearance and therefore must be a U.S. citizen.

Preferred Qualifications

The following are not requirements but would bring significant value to the team:

  • Experience supporting business development, capture management, pipeline management, gate reviews, or proposal-to-execution transitions.
  • Experience contributing to competitive proposals through solution development, win strategy, competitive differentiation, cost optimization, or the development of proposal discriminators.
  • Experience identifying and leveraging existing organizational capabilities, reusable solutions, past performance, or repeatable service offerings to strengthen proposals and improve business outcomes.
  • Experience developing or coordinating Basis of Estimates (BOEs), cost estimates, resource estimates, or similar inputs supporting business proposals.
  • Experience working within a large, matrixed organization supporting multiple lines of business, programs, or customers.
  • Experience supporting Information Assurance, Cybersecurity, Secure IT, or other National Security environments.
  • Working knowledge of the Risk Management Framework (RMF), Authority to Operate (ATO) processes, government cybersecurity requirements, or regulatory compliance.
  • Experience planning or coordinating classified or secure IT infrastructure, including workstations, servers, applications, networks, cloud or AI services.
  • Experience ordering, moving, or coordinating government network circuits and working across government and industry stakeholders to drive long-lead connectivity activities to completion.
  • Experience supporting secure facility planning, construction, accreditation, relocation, or infrastructure transition activities.
  • Experience developing new organizational processes, governance mechanisms, metrics, and operating rhythms where mature processes did not previously exist.

We know that true impact comes from personalization and an unwavering commitment to serve patients and expand the possibilities of life-prolonging oncology medicines.

About the Role

The Manager, Market Access Operations makes sure Secura Bio's pricing, 340B, government programs, contracting and channel operations are accurate, compliant and run well. This person is the operations lead for the Market Access team within Commercial Operations. They work with Finance and the government pricing vendor to coordinate and check pricing calculations and submissions. The role manages the 340B program day to day, along with contract operations and channel partners, and provides market access insights to the Commercial team. This is a remote position.

Employment Type

Full-time

Reports To

Executive Director, Commercial Operations & Analytics

Key Responsibilities

Pricing Management

  • Coordinate list price (WAC) changes from approval through implementation.
  • Send pricing notices to drug pricing databases (such as Medi-Span, First Databank and Red Book), channel partners and customers on time.
  • Manage state drug price transparency reporting and advance notices of price increases. Keep a calendar of state requirements.
  • Work with Finance to model the impact of pricing decisions on gross-to-net, government programs and inflation rebates.
  • Maintain the pricing governance documents, price history and approval records.

Government Pricing Coordination

  • Serve as the main operations contact with Finance and the outside vendor for monthly and quarterly government price calculations and submissions. These include AMP, Best Price, ASP, Non-FAMP and Federal Ceiling Price.
  • Collaborate with Finance in support of sales, contract and chargeback data that feed the calculations. Make sure it is complete and accurate.
  • Review vendor results for accuracy and unusual changes. Investigate differences and record findings before submissions are approved.
  • Manage the reporting calendar so all deadlines are met.
  • Support Medicaid Drug Rebate Program, VA FSS and TRICARE operations, including rebate invoice validation, dispute resolution and contract coordination.
  • Help keep government pricing policies, methods and assumptions documented and current, with Finance, Legal and Compliance.
  • Track regulatory changes, such as Inflation Reduction Act inflation rebates and CMS guidance, and flag operational impacts.

340B Program Management

  • Manage Secura Bio's 340B program day to day, in line with HRSA requirements and company policy.
  • Work with Finance and the vendor to check 340B ceiling prices each quarter. Confirm they are correctly loaded into the government's 340B pricing system and wholesaler systems.
  • Monitor how 340B prices are applied through chargebacks. Investigate pricing errors, refunds and restatements.
  • Monitor 340B purchasing and contract pharmacy activity. Coordinate with vendors on claims data and on identifying duplicate discounts with Medicaid.
  • Support 340B policy decisions, audits of covered entities, disputes and HRSA inquiries, with Legal and Compliance.
  • Keep 340B documentation audit-ready and track legal and regulatory changes.

Contracting and Gross-to-Net

  • Manage how payer, specialty pharmacy, distributor and GPO contracts are carried out, including fee-for-service, data fees, rebates, chargebacks and administrative fees.
  • Validate rebate claims, chargebacks and fee invoices. Resolve disputes.
  • Work with Finance on gross-to-net forecasting, accruals and month-end close. Explain differences between forecast and actual.
  • Keep the contract inventory current and track key terms, renewals and obligations.

Channel and Patient Access Operations

  • Manage service agreements, onboarding and performance (against agreed service levels) for specialty pharmacies, specialty distributors and wholesalers.
  • Track inventory, order patterns and product availability across the channel.
  • Provide operational oversight of the hub and patient support programs, including benefits verification, prior authorization, copay assistance and free goods. Track time to therapy and abandonment.

Data, Reporting and Insights

  • Own the quality of market access data (channel, hub, 340B, chargebacks and rebates). Work with vendors and Analytics to fix issues.

  • Provide insights and recommendations to Market Access and Commercial leadership.
  • Manage HCP and Account affiliation data mapping tables and site of care mix across parent accounts and weekly data change process.

Vendors, Compliance and Process

  • Manage the government pricing, 340B, channel data and hub vendors, including scopes of work, deliverables, budgets and performance reviews.

  • Support internal and external audits. Ensure compliance with federal and state requirements, with Legal, Compliance and Finance.

Required Qualifications

  • Hands-on experience with a manufacturer's 340B program, including ceiling prices, chargebacks, contract pharmacy and compliance

Job Description:

GDIT is seeking a Sr. Principal RF/Spectrum Systems Engineer to support Counter Unmanned Aircraft Systems (CUAS) engineering for the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA). In this high-impact role, you will lead the research, testing, evaluation, and spectrum analysis of cutting-edge UAS detection and mitigation technologies in active airport environments.

This position uniquely bridges hands-on RF engineering, advanced systems analysis, and national policy development—directly influencing future FAA Advisory Circulars and aviation safety standards.

Key Responsibilities

RF & Radar Engineering

  • Lead radar testing across L, S, C, X, Ku, and Ka frequency bands using FMCW, pulse Doppler, and other waveforms (including Phased Array antenna technologies).
  • Lead testing of mitigation devices operating in other frequency bands (VHF/UHF/Microwave).
  • Conduct precise RF measurements (power, gain, EIRP, spectrum occupancy) and evaluate electromagnetic compatibility (EM/EMC) for spectral compliance.
  • Perform near-field and far-field antenna range measurements in controlled or operational environments.

CUAS Research, Testing & Evaluation (RD/T&E)

  • Conduct rigorous spectrum interference testing at active airports prior to CUAS deployment.
  • Develop, execute, and oversee detailed test plans, test cards, and structured evaluation frameworks.
  • Manage vendor systems during deployment, troubleshooting, data collection, and teardown.
  • Establish selection criteria for UAS platforms used in evaluations, alongside performance metrics and pass/fail criteria.
  • Document all RD/T&E activities to contribute to FAA guidance on the selection, procurement, deployment, and management of CUAS systems as well as RF-specific measurement equipment.

Systems Engineering & Strategic Policy

  • Conduct thorough RF hazard analyses and safety assessments prior to open-air testing.
  • Translate complex RD/T&E data into performance specification frameworks using modeling, simulation, and analysis tools to shape FAA Advisory Circulars.
  • Utilize technical data tools to model and analyze spectrum environments and system capabilities.
  • Create multi-airport CUAS operational recommendations and best practices aligned with FAA Safety Risk Management (SRM) principles.

Qualifications Required:

  • Bachelor of Engineering degree in Electrical, Aerospace, Systems, Mechanical (preferred) or other technical discipline. Non-U.S. degrees must be ABET accredited.
  • 10+ years of progressive engineering experience in RF, radar, or spectrum management.
  • Proven experience using spectrum analyzers and other equipment to test, evaluate and characterize complex RF devices and environments for FCC/NTIA compliance.
  • Demonstrated success in conducting open-air RF/spectrum data collection.
  • Ability to evaluate the functional capabilities of complex technologies with minimal supervision.
  • Highly collaborative with strong technical writing and presentation skills for both technical and non-technical audiences with teams including other disciplines.
  • Ability to independently plan and deliver projects with high-quality, on-time results.
  • Proficiency with MS Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
  • Physical ability to lift up to 25 lbs. during field deployments.
  • Ability to obtain an FAA Suitability clearance and maintain a valid U.S. passport.

Preferred:

  • Direct experience developing or executing structured test plans for aviation or defense technologies.
  • Proficiency with data analysis and visualization tools (e.g., MATLAB, Python, JMP, or advanced Excel).
  • Familiarity with FAA Safety Risk Management (SRM) principles or airport operations.

Growth & Experimentation Manager -Full Time (Remote)

Our Organization

CDP, a Boston-based public benefit corporation, uses the collaborative fundraising model to improve the operational efficiency and revenue generation capacity of the public media system. CDP currently provides more than 230 NPR and PBS stations with outsourced marketing, data analytics, fundraising, and technology services. These services help stations raise more net income, grow their donor files faster, lower their fundraising costs, and free up development talent allowing stations to better focus on local engagement. Since its inception, CDP has driven $1 billion in incremental net value back to stations and has become the most widely adopted station service in the history of public broadcasting.

Just as CDP is committed to supporting public media organizations around the country, we are equally committed to supporting each of our team in their own professional development. For more information visit

Department Overview:

The Strategic Marketing & Fundraising Services Team (SMFS) team delivers data-driven scalable fundraising programs that strengthen donor relationships and maximize long-term results for partner stations in the mail and digital fundraising spaces. Through strategic planning, creative development, cross-functional collaboration, and continuous testing and performance optimization, the team develops and executes customized direct mail and digital strategies aligned with each station’s brand, goals, and fundraising priorities.

Position Overview:

Reporting to the Director, Digital Marketing Fundraiser & Strategy, the Growth & Experimentation Manager builds, launches, and optimizes growth experiments across digital fundraising channels—including email, forms, paid media, and emerging channels. This role focuses on testing new ideas quickly, translating concepts into tangible digital experiences, and applying learnings to improve fundraising and business outcomes.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Build, launch, and optimize growth experiments across digital fundraising channels, including emails, forms, ads, and other channels, with a focus on testing new ideas quickly and implementing learnings. Partner with mail and digital leadership to
  • Prioritize and execute a shared testing roadmap, balancing priorities set by leadership with experiment ideas of your own.
  • Partner with the Associate Director, Digital Fundraising Strategy, the Principal Data Solutions Engineer, and the Sr. Digital Marketing Developer to turn concepts into tangible digital experiences, tools, campaigns, and workflows in Iterable, PushPlanet, SpringBoard, Snowflake, and other platforms.
  • Lead the development and testing of new digital fundraising tools and campaigns, AI tools, platforms, integrations, and digital capabilities, including PushPlanet and subforms, SMS, paid media initiatives, and emerging tools.
  • Work cross-functionally with creative, digital (email and forms), analytics and data, and Client Success teams to bring experiments to life.
  • Analyze experiment results and translate findings into actionable recommendations, optimizations, and opportunities for future testing.
  • Identify opportunities to improve, streamline, or automate existing processes and workflows, including evaluating project management and other operational tools, and coordinate implementation of process improvements with the relevant teams.
  • Stay curious about emerging trends in digital fundraising, marketing technology, paid acquisition, conversion optimization, and AI, and assess their potential application to our work.
  • Document experiments, results, and learnings in an Asana project to create a shared knowledge base of what works—and what does not—and help establish a repeatable test → learn → iterate → scale framework for digital fundraising innovation.
  • Identify successful experiments and develop recommendations and implementation plans for scaling proven approaches across campaigns, channels, and stations. Establish repeatable processes and documentation that enable successful tests to be adopted beyond the original pilot.
  • Evaluate experiments against fundraising and business outcomes, including conversion rates, response rates, revenue, acquisition costs, donor value, and operational efficiency, where applicable.
  • Champion inclusion and a supportive culture in all aspects of work, modeling these values across the organization.

  • 5-7 years of demonstrated experience designing, executing, measuring, and iterating on marketing or digital growth experiments.

  • Technical aptitude and the ability to learn new platforms, integrations, and marketing technologies quickly.
  • Experience with digital fundraising, conversion rate optimization, marketing automation, landing pages, forms, or related digital marketing capabilities.
  • Familiarity with analytics and data tools, including tracking implementation, event measurement, and performance reporting.
  • Ability to translate business challenges into practical technical solutions and collaborate effectively with technical and nontechnical teams.· Strong project management skills, including prioritization, documentation, and management of multiple concurrent initiatives.

We value diverse perspectives, lived experiences, and commitment to public service. All CDP people have unique talents and experiences that create our company culture where we can all thrive and bring our whole selves to work each day.

Owner Success Specialist – Customer Support (Spanish Speaker)

Remote | Freelance / Independent Contractor | Spain Working Hours

About GuestReady

GuestReady is a leading short-term rental and hospitality management company operating across multiple markets, including the UK, France, Portugal, Spain and the UAE.

Since 2016, we have combined technology with high-quality hospitality services to help property owners get the most out of their properties and deliver excellent guest experiences.

We are looking for an English-speaking Owner Support Specialist to join our UK Owner Success team. This is a fully remote opportunity offered on a freelance/independent contractor basis, requiring availability during UK business hours.

Role Overview

As an Owner Support Specialist, you will be one of the main points of contact for property owners, providing day-to-day support and ensuring their questions, requests and concerns are handled efficiently and professionally.

Your main responsibilities will include answering incoming calls, managing support tickets, responding to emails and coordinating with internal teams to resolve owner-related issues.

You will play an important role in delivering an excellent owner experience by ensuring timely communication, effective problem-solving and proper follow-up on all requests.

Key Responsibilities

  • Owner Communication: Handle incoming calls, emails and support requests from property owners, providing clear, friendly and professional assistance.

  • Ticket Management: Manage and respond to owner support tickets through our internal systems, ensuring requests are properly tracked, prioritised and resolved within expected timelines.

  • Issue Resolution: Investigate owner questions and concerns, provide accurate information and find appropriate solutions.

  • Internal Coordination: Work closely with Operations, Guest Experience, Finance and Account Management teams to resolve issues and ensure smooth communication.

  • Escalation Management: Identify complex or sensitive situations and escalate them to the appropriate teams or Account Managers when necessary.

  • Follow-up: Ensure owners receive timely updates on their requests and that outstanding issues are followed through to resolution.

  • CRM & Documentation: Keep accurate records of owner interactions, support tickets and resolutions in our CRM and internal platforms.

  • Owner Experience: Build positive relationships with property owners by providing reliable, empathetic and solution-oriented support.

  • Continuous Improvement: Identify recurring issues and suggest improvements to internal processes and the overall owner support experience.

What We're Looking For

  • Previous experience in Customer Support, Customer Service, Owner Support or a similar client-facing role.

  • Native Spanish and fluent English: communication skills, both written and spoken.

  • Comfortable handling a high volume of incoming calls, emails and support tickets.

  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to handle difficult conversations professionally.

  • A customer-focused mindset and a genuine interest in helping people.

  • Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage multiple requests and priorities simultaneously.

  • Good problem-solving skills and attention to detail.

  • Confidence using CRM platforms, ticketing systems and digital tools.

  • Ability to work independently in a remote environment while collaborating with an international team.

  • Availability to work Spanish business hours.

  • Availability to work some weekends.

Nice to have:

  • Experience in short-term rentals, property management, hospitality or proptech.

  • Previous experience using HubSpot, Zendesk or similar customer support platforms.

  • Experience supporting international customers or clients.

Please note: This is a customer support role focused on handling owner requests and resolving day-to-day issues. Previous experience managing a commercial portfolio of accounts is not required.

Contract

This opportunity is offered on a freelance/independent contractor basis and is open to candidates who can work remotely during UK business hours.

You will provide services to GuestReady as an independent contractor rather than as an employee, on a full-time basis.

Further details regarding the working schedule, compensation and collaboration model will be discussed during the recruitment process.

Why Work With GuestReady?

  • Join an international, multicultural team in the travel and hospitality industry.

  • Enjoy the flexibility of working remotely.

  • Gain experience in a fast-growing, technology-driven hospitality company.

  • Collaborate with colleagues across different countries and departments.

  • Develop your customer support and problem-solving skills in an international environment.

  • Be part of a supportive team that values collaboration, ownership and continuous improvement.

Join Us

GuestReady is committed to creating an inclusive environment and welcomes applications from people with diverse backgrounds, experiences and perspectives.

If you enjoy helping people, solving problems and delivering excellent customer service, we'd love to hear from you!

En tant que marque en pleine croissance, principalement en ligne, notre succès repose sur une équipe qui partage notre passion pour redéfinir l’expérience des meubles.

La mission du ou de la Gestionnaire de l’expérience et de la formation en commerce de détail chez Cozey

Relevant du Vice-président de la stratégie et des opérations de commerce de détail, vous façonnerez la manière dont nos équipes en magasin apprennent, dirigent et offrent une expérience client exceptionnelle.

Alors que Cozey continue d’élargir sa présence en magasin, vous bâtirez les programmes de coaching et de formation qui développeront des leaders confiant.e.s, rehausseront les comportements de vente et donneront vie à l’expérience de notre marque dans chacun de nos magasins. Une solide base de formation sur les produits est déjà en place. Vous vous concentrerez donc sur le développement de nos leaders en tant que coachs, sur la création d’une culture d’apprentissage continu et sur la transformation de la formation en résultats concrets.

Ce poste est en télétravail et ouvert partout au Canada. Vous devez résider près de l’un de nos magasins Cozey, soit à Edmonton, Calgary, Toronto, Montréal ou Vancouver, et prévoir environ 25 à 30 % de déplacements.

Ce que vous ferez

  • Bâtir un programme de coaching évolutif qui permet aux gérant.e.s de magasin, aux gérant.e.s adjoint.e.s et aux détenteur.rice.s de clés de devenir de meilleur.e.s coachs, de donner de la rétroaction constructive et d’aborder les conversations difficiles avec assurance.
  • Donner vie à la philosophie de vente de Cozey en traduisant les attentes en matière d’expérience client en comportements quotidiens qui renforcent le lien avec les client.e.s et rehaussent l’expérience en magasin.

Fullsteam is a leading provider of vertical software and embedded payments technology dedicated to helping businesses flourish by providing their customers with seamless experiences. Join us and be a part of a forward-thinking company that values growth, excellence, and the success of our clients.

At Commerce7, part of the Fullsteam organization, we believe that above price and product, the number one reason why a consumer chooses a brand is customer experience. Customer experiences that are customer-centric lead to loyalty, customer happiness, and ultimately drive sales and profit. Our mission at Commerce7 is to empower wineries with the tools and insights needed to deliver exceptional customer experiences and succeed in DTC.


At Commerce7, the moments that bring wineries together, like a packed webinar, a well-run tradeshow, or a dinner that people remember, are where relationships are built. The Marketing Coordinator (Events) makes those moments happen. Working with Marketing, Sales, and RevOps, you coordinate the logistics, vendors, and operational execution that turn great events into pipeline and lasting customer connections.


Great events happen when planning is given the time it needs. You’ll work backward from each event date, build in room for strategy, planning, and approvals, and flag risks early so there’s always time to adjust. Leadership owns strategy, event selection, budget, and contracts.


Primary Responsibilities:

  • Own logistics for approved trade shows, conferences, webinars, and customer events, including registrations, travel arrangements, shipping, schedules, and onsite support.
  • Prepare booth assets, branded merchandise, presentations, and attendee communications; confirm vendor requirements and arrange approved services.
  • Track event expenses, process invoices, and flag budget discrepancies; obtain approval for changes to pricing, services, or contracts.
  • Build and run checklists, timeline and run-of-show, and flag risks early.
  • Coordinate the production and delivery of event promotional assets, including emails, digital content, and social media materials.
  • Coordinate sales collateral, promotional materials, and approved sponsorship or co-marketing activities with Sales, Customer Success, and Partnerships.
  • Support event and campaign lead capture, check contact details, and route leads for timely follow-up using established handoff processes.
  • Maintain contact records, campaign tracking, and event documentation in the CRM and marketing automation tools, following established data and consent procedures.
  • Schedule customer meetings, manage booth schedules, and gather collateral needs from Sales, Customer Success, and Partnerships.
  • Maintain calendars, timelines, checklists, and task trackers across assigned projects; coordinate meetings, agendas, status updates, and stakeholder communications.
  • Compile post-event reports for marketing leadership, including attendance, demos, spend, and other event metrics. Document lessons learned and update event playbooks.

Skills & Competencies:

  • Keeps many moving parts straight at once, such as registrations, shipping, travel, vendor deadlines, and run-of-show. Builds checklists and timelines without being asked, and raises risks early rather than at load-in.
  • Tracks spend against budget, reads a quote or invoice carefully, and flags variances. Knows to escalate any change in price, scope, or contract terms rather than approving it.
  • Comfortable representing Commerce7 at trade shows and events. Warm, professional, and views work through the lens of hospitality.
  • Writes concise briefs and status updates. Works well with Sales, RevOps, Customer Success, and external vendors, and closes the loop without being chased.
  • Works independently within established event processes and escalates decisions regarding strategy, budgets, contracts, or significant event changes to leadership.
  • Takes feedback well, runs a post-event debrief, and turns lessons into better checklists for the next event.
  • Clearly manages internal communications and planning via Slack and internal meetings as necessary.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • 1–3 years of experience in event coordination, marketing, or a related field, including support for events, campaigns, or projects.
  • Degree or diploma in Marketing, Communications, Business, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Experience using a CRM such as HubSpot, Salesforce, or a similar platform to maintain contacts or track campaign activity.
  • Proficiency with spreadsheets, presentations, and collaboration tools in Microsoft Office or Google Workspace.

Preferred Qualifications
