jobs.excerpt: *CANDIDATES MUST BE LOCATED IN THE UNITED STATES** About SafelyYou SafelyYou’s passionate mission is to empower safer, more person-centered care across senior living through world-leading AI, industry-changing hardware, and remote expert clinicians, significantly improving outcomes for residents while increasing peace of mind for families and reducing costs for communities.
jobs.description:
*CANDIDATES MUST BE LOCATED IN THE UNITED STATES**

About SafelyYou

SafelyYou’s passionate mission is to empower safer, more person-centered care across senior living through world-leading AI, industry-changing hardware, and remote expert clinicians, significantly improving outcomes for residents while increasing peace of mind for families and reducing costs for communities.

Originating in 2015 as the doctoral research of CEO George Netscher—and inspired by his own family's experience with Alzheimer's disease—SafelyYou was spun out of UC Berkeley’s Artificial Intelligence Research Lab, one of the top five AI research groups in the world. And today, our company is solving critical challenges in senior living, from resident falls and ER visits to staffing concerns, length of stay, and NOI. All helping ensure that communities can focus on improved care for residents while still reaching their financial goals.

SafelyYou is one of five most innovative fall technologies referenced in the Senate Falls Report (2019), a winner of the McKnight’s Tech Partner of the Year, and has been named to Fortune’s Impact 20 list, which recognizes companies making people’s lives better through innovation.

Your Role at SafelyYou
The Install Coordinator serves as the operational backbone of the installation process, ensuring seamless execution of SafelyYou’s in-room sensor deployments while Implementation Managers focus on customer-facing responsibilities. This role acts as a bridge between the Implementation Managers, Implementation Agents, and field technicians providing real-time support, resolving install blockers, and maintaining installation accuracy, timeliness, and quality.

At SafelyYou, the work you do truly matters. Our mission to protect and empower older adults is at the heart of everything we build and deliver. You’ll be part of a team that believes technology can make care more human; creating safer, calmer, and more connected communities for residents, caregivers, and families alike.

You will play a key part in ensuring that every SafelyYou deployment meets our high standards of excellence, supporting both new installations and ongoing expansions across the customer base.

Key Responsibilities:

Installation Support & Coordination

  • Manage day-to-day install operations for all active installations, including tracking progress, coordinating schedules, and resolving blockers.

  • Handle installation escalations flagged by Implementation Agents such as late or damaged shipments, unique room layouts requiring special mounting consideration, alternate cable routing, inaccessible power outlets, or inaccessible mounting locations.

  • Conduct virtual walkthroughs with community maintenance teams or field technicians to confirm sensor placement and validate completed installations.

  • Perform quality checks for sensor view and IR settings upon completion of each installation to ensure full system functionality.

  • Coordinate with field technicians to complete post-sale Wi-Fi assessments of customer buildings, ensuring network readiness for installation and identifying any connectivity concerns in advance.

  • Coordinate with vendors and shipping teams to ensure timely and accurate delivery of all equipment.

  • Submit work orders for installations to vendor partners, monitor progress through completion, and verify adherence to SafelyYou’s documentation requirements and installation standards. Provide proactive communication and support to ensure timely resolution of any field issues or delays.

  • Occasional travel required; up to 25%

Cross-Functional Liaison

  • Collaborate with Implementation Agents and field technicians to manage install progress and resolve issues while Implementation Managers are customer-facing, maintaining clear communication, alignment on priorities, and shared task ownership.

  • Provide IA team with clear escalation paths and documentation standards to ensure accurate issue tracking in Salesforce or other systems.

  • Communicate install updates, delays, and resolutions to the Implementation Manager and other stakeholders in real time.

  • Collaborate with Solutions team to ensure building readiness prior to installation.

  • Escalate to Support as needed for troubleshooting during installation.

System & Data Management

  • Verify post-install sensor connectivity and accuracy; document outcomes and flag discrepancies.

  • Add and maintain all installation documentation in customer folders to ensure accuracy, consistency, and easy access for internal stakeholders.

  • Oversee data entry and workflow management in Salesforce, ensuring install milestones and statuses are up to date.

  • Partner with Procurement to monitor equipment inventory and proactively identify low-stock or delayed shipments.

Process Improvement

  • Identify recurring install pain points and propose improvements to process, tooling, or field workflows.

  • Partner with leadership to refine the install playbook, standardize documentation templates, and support onboarding of new Implementation Agents or field technicians.

The Ideal Candidate:

  • 2–4 years of experience in project coordination, field operations, or technical implementation, ideally in a SaaS, healthcare environment paired with physical hardware deployment experience.

  • Experience with structured cabling or RF technology a bonus.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer
jobs.excerpt: Join ICOMAT – Revolutionising the Future of Lightweight Manufacturing!
jobs.description:
Join ICOMAT – Revolutionising the Future of Lightweight Manufacturing!

iCOMAT is an advanced manufacturing company that invented Rapid Tow Shearing (RTS) - the only proven technology for producing defect-free curved-fiber composite parts at industrial scale. We deliver the lightest structures possible for aerospace, automotive, defense, and space, at a rate and cost efficiency that far exceeds existing composite production processes.

We build and operate automated factories for composite materials, delivering components to Tier 1 suppliers and OEMs. The business has three main divisions: development of automated production machines, development of software design and production tools, and operation of the factory. We work with 25+ customers and completed the largest ever Series A in composites manufacturing to fuel a significant scale-up, with growth plans that will see the business multiply in size over the next two to three years and expand operations into the UK, Europe and the US.

The business has currently more than 130,000 sqm of production capacity with manufacturing facilities in the UK (Gloucester and Swindon) and the US (Dayton, Ohio); a Hardware R&D Centre in Bristol, UK; and a Software R&D Centre in Athens, Greece.

We are hiring Senior Software Engineers to join our in-house Software Engineering team and build iCOMAT’s manufacturing and business operations system. This platform is iCOMAT’s central hub for executing R&D and manufacturing activities, connecting ERP, production scheduling, machine telemetry, shop-floor execution and business operations across our manufacturing sites.

What will you be doing?

From day one, you will be building and shipping systems that are used daily by planners, manufacturing engineers, and R&D teams to run real factories.

The software platform is built on a modern web-stack and runs entirely using on-prem infrastructure, with cloud adoption ramping up in 2027. All aspects of iCOMAT’s business and manufacturing activities are within scope, from ERP and SaaS integrations to real-time telemetry streams from the machines on our production floor. The goal is to provide a real-time view of our factories that enables autonomous decision making to deliver high quality, repeatable composite manufacturing at scale.

Depending on your strengths, your focus will sit across one or more of the platform's three pillars:

  1. Web application development. Building production-grade, full-stack features in Nuxt, TypeScript and Postgres, including asynchronous and event-driven workloads (queues, Pub/Sub) and real-time interfaces over websockets.

  2. Data orchestration. Designing and operating data pipelines and warehousing (BigQuery or similar) with orchestration frameworks such as Dagster, Airflow or Prefect, in Python.

  3. Agent Development and Orchestration. Deploying autonomous agents that integrate with ICOMAT’s business systems and operating context to power AI-enabled decision making across the business.

As well as writing software code, you will be expected to contribute across much of the software development lifecycle, from co-designing requirements with end users on the factory floor, to validating MVPs, and executing the build, test and release of production-standard software.

What does success look like?

As a manufacturing business, our success is defined by the quality of the parts we produce, the repeatability of our manufacturing processes, and the reliability of the operations behind them.

iCOMAT’s business and manufacturing platform builds on this by giving our teams a single, trusted view of the factory — replacing fragile spreadsheets and disconnected tools with software that makes scheduling, execution, and reporting faster, clearer, and dependable.

From a personal perspective, we value engineers who can turn ambiguous operational problems into robust software systems, communicate clearly with technical and non-technical stakeholders, and deliver production-quality tools that are trusted by the business.

iCOMAT is setting the standard for how advanced composite structures are designed, manufactured, and industrialised at scale. Your contributions will build the operational backbone for world-leading technology that will be embedded in the next generation of aerospace and defence hardware.

How do you fit in?

You will be joining iCOMAT's in-house software engineering team, reporting directly to the Head of AI and working alongside other Senior Software Engineers. This is a small, senior team developing the software foundations for iCOMAT's design, manufacturing, and operations capability.

The current team brings experience across manufacturing and engineering, machine learning and production-grade software delivery. We work closely with iCOMAT's planning, manufacturing engineering, and production teams to understand the problems that matter most, then turn those problems into reliable internal products.

This role would suit someone who enjoys contributing to a team where the boundaries between product thinking, engineering judgement, and software delivery are deliberately close.

For this role, your contribution will be to deepen the team's capability across full-stack web development, data engineering, and cloud/platform operations — and to help set the engineering standards for a platform that the whole business will come to depend on. You will bring practical software engineering discipline, curiosity about manufacturing operations, and the confidence to collaborate with domain experts to build software that is robust, maintainable, and genuinely useful.

Who you are?

Innovative. You are comfortable developing novel solutions for truly complex problems.

Independent.You don't shy away from open-ended problems and enjoy helping shape end-to-end solutions. You are comfortable working as an individual contributor as part of a multi-functional team.

Product-minded. Software is more than just code. You embrace the opportunity to contribute across the end-to-end software development lifecycle and care about delivering a solution that creates real, measurable value for the business.

Operations-led. You enjoy working close to the realities of a live production environment — scheduling constraints, machine data, shop-floor workflows — and you are motivated by building software that helps a factory run better every day.

What should you expect?

iCOMAT is on a mission to revolutionise the way engineers design and manufacture with composite materials. We have a build-first methodology and take pride in developing in-house capabilities that cater for our specific needs. Our technology is world-leading, and our software must be capable of supporting demanding operational workflows from the planning office through to the production floor.

You should expect to work on problems where software, data, manufacturing, and product thinking meet. This role will suit someone who enjoys writing high-quality code but also wants to understand how that code changes the way a real factory operates.

iCOMAT is fast paced. The atmosphere is demanding but rewarding. We are operating at the cutting edge of composite manufacturing technology, and we are looking for people who want to help build the operational software foundations that allow that technology to scale.

Our Stack

  • Full Stack Framework: Nuxt

  • Application Database: Postgres

  • Data Orchestration: Currently evaluating Dagster, Prefect and Airflow

  • AI Tooling: Claude Code

  • Version Control & CI/CD: Self-Hosted GitLab

  • Languages: Typescript, Python (bonus points for Go, C++, C#, Julia)

  • Application Hosting: On-prem, docker-based deployments

  • Cloud: GCP & Azure (GCP preferred for new workflows)

Skills and Experience

Essential

  • 5+ years of demonstrable industry experience building and operating production software systems used by real end users

  • 5+ years hands-on software development experience in TypeScript and/or Python. We also value experience in Go, C# and C++.

  • Deep, hands-on expertise in at least two of the platform's three pillars: full-stack web development (Nuxt/Vue or comparable modern framework, Postgres, async/event-driven patterns, websockets); data orchestration (data warehousing such as BigQuery, plus Dagster, Airflow or Prefect); cloud computing (AWS, Azure or GCP; GCP preferred)

  • Solid working knowledge of relational databases, including schema design, migrations, and query performance (Postgres preferred)

  • Familiarity with modern software development practices, such as test-driven development, automated testing, code review, CI/CD, and containerisation

  • Strong first-degree or Masters/PhD in computer science or a STEM-related subject

  • Eligible to work with UK export-controlled material and willing to undergo security screening if required

Desirable

  • Previous start-up or scale-up experience is highly advantageous – we move very fast

  • Experience working in aerospace & defence, manufacturing or logistics

  • Experience developing software for highly regulated and/or export-controlled environments

  • Experience developing software to comply with common information management and cyber security certifications (e.g. ISO 27001, SOC 2, etc.)

  • Experience integrating with ERP, MES, or other manufacturing/business systems

  • Experience with industrial data protocols and telemetry (e.g. MQTT, OPC-UA) or other high-volume event streams

  • Working knowledge of C# / .NET – some engineering systems run this stack

  • Experience deploying and operating software in self-hosted / on-prem environments

  • Experience developing accessible and intuitive user experiences across a variety of design tools and front-end frameworks

  • Experience developing agentic tools for use by end-users

  • Comfortable using AI coding tools such as Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, or similar developer assistants

  • Experience applying machine learning in production environments (e.g. AI Engineer, MLOps, Data Science)

Our Values: Uncompromising Excellence

  • Discipline over excuses. We commit. We follow through. We hold ourselves and each other to the highest standard, especially when the pressure is on.

  • Push the edge. iCOMAT was built on a refusal to accept that curved fiber could not be manufactured at scale. We innovate where others hesitate.

  • Aligned and accountable. Everyone owns their lane, communicates openly, and delivers without being chased. No silos. No ambiguity.

Why iCOMAT?

  • Competitive Salary & Benefits: We offer a comprehensive benefits package, including private healthcare, pension scheme.

  • Stock Options: Equity options to give employees a stake in the company’s success

  • Career Growth Opportunities: Join us at a pivotal time as we scale up, offering unmatched professional growth opportunities in the rapidly advancing field of composite materials.

  • Innovation-Focused Culture: We pride ourselves on our inclusive, forward-thinking work environment. Recognized by Bloomberg as a "UK Startup to Watch," iCOMAT celebrates diversity and encourages all applicants, regardless of background, to apply.

  • Global Impact: Be a part of our mission to redefine lightweight structures for the automotive, aerospace, and space industries, working with some of the most influential companies worldwide.Ready to be part of something big?

Apply now to learn more and join us on our exciting journey!

Who We Are

Arpio is building the next generation of disaster recovery (DR) for the cloud.

Modern enterprises face a growing list of threats to their cloud applications. With the increasing complexity of cloud-native environments, we know resilience to these threats is about more than just data. That's why, at Arpio, we have built a best in class SaaS offering that makes it easier than ever to protect your entire cloud infrastructure across AWS and Azure from catastrophic downtime.

About the Role

Most companies don't think seriously about disaster recovery…until they have to. Ransomware hits. A cloud region goes dark. An audit looms. That's where we come in. As an Arpio SDR, you'll own the top of the funnel for a platform that protects businesses from catastrophic data loss across both AWS and Azure environments. You'll prospect into IT and security teams, surface the gaps in their current backup posture, and book meetings that turn into real pipeline. This is a role with real ownership and real influence on how we grow. Your work directly funds our next stage of growth.

What You'll Do

Generate Pipeline

  • Run high-volume, high-quality outbound via cold call, email, and LinkedIn, targeting IT Directors, CISOs, and infrastructure owners across AWS and Azure environments
  • Build and execute personalized multi-touch sequences tailored to DR-specific pain (Disaster Recovery): ransomware exposure, compliance deadlines, migration risk, and multi-cloud complexity
  • Qualify inbound leads quickly and accurately, routing the right opportunities to AEs with full context
  • Follow up on events, webinars, and content downloads to convert intent into booked meetings
  • Expectations: Maintain high daily call volume (150+ dials/day) and optimal call time to consistently achieve a target of 6 Sales Qualified Leads (SQLs) per month

Run Sharp Discovery

  • Ask the questions that uncover real urgency like current RTO/RPO targets, last DR test date, compliance obligations, recent incidents, and which cloud platform(s) house their critical workloads
  • Map stakeholders across IT, security, and finance since DR decisions rarely live with a single person
  • Pass qualified meetings to AEs with documented pain points, stakeholder context, and relevant use case, not just a calendar invite; take end-to-end relationship ownership with Account Executives by attending booked meetings and driving joint success

Build the Foundation

  • Log all activity accurately in the CRM (HubSpot), maintain clean pipeline hygiene, and produce weekly reports detailing top-of-the-funnel additions and outbound activity campaigns to drive self-accountability
  • Test messaging, track what resonates, and feed insights back to marketing and leadership
  • Share what's working with messaging, objections, competitive intel, because the whole team moves faster when knowledge isn't siloed
  • Help build the outbound playbook from the ground up — including messaging that speaks credibly to Azure buyers as well as AWS buyers

Must-Haves

Experience & Background

  • Minimum 1.5 years of SDR/BDR, inside sales, or quota-carrying outbound experience in a SaaS B2B environment
  • Prior experience prospecting into or selling to technical buyers in cloud infrastructure, security, or IT operations
  • Working knowledge of cloud infrastructure (e.g., compute, storage, networking) sufficient to speak credibly with IT and security buyers about cloud resilience; AWS or Azure familiarity is a strong plus

Skills & Competencies

  • Proven comfort with outbound prospecting including phone, email, LinkedIn, and multichannel sequences
  • Outstanding verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills with the ability to educate and persuade diverse audiences
  • Proficiency with sales tools: HubSpot, Nooks, SmartLead, Walaxy (for LinkedIn automation)
  • Strong grit and analytical skills to evaluate outreach metrics, understand performance drivers, and optimize prospecting actions independently

How You Work

At Arpio, we care about the outcome as much as the effort it took to get there. We take initiative, follow through, and report back on what we learned along the way. That same instinct shows up in how we treat customers and each other: we respond quickly, speak honestly and openly, and trust our teammates to take direct feedback as a chance to grow. We move like a startup because we are one, spending wisely and treating every dollar and every customer like they matter, because they do. If that's how you like to work, you'll fit in well here. In this role it’s especially important that you:

jobs.excerpt: Position Summary The Business Continuity Manager is a key role responsible for overseeing the development and implementation of business continuity plans to ensure the company’s operations can withstand and recover from unexpected disruptions.
jobs.description:
Position Summary

The Business Continuity Manager is a key role responsible for overseeing the development and implementation of business continuity plans to ensure the company’s operations can withstand and recover from unexpected disruptions.

What will your job entail?

Job Responsibilities:

  • Assess the potential impact of disruptions on critical business processes, identifying dependencies, recovery time objectives (RTOs), and resource requirements.
  • Identify and evaluate risks that could affect business operations, including natural disasters, cyber threats, supply chain disruptions, and other emergencies. Develop strategies to mitigate these risks.
  • Create and maintain comprehensive emergency response plans that outline procedures for handling crises, evacuations, communication, and resource allocation during disruptions.
  • Develop and update business continuity plans (BCPs) that address various scenarios, ensuring alignment with organizational goals and compliance requirements.
  • Coordinate regular testing and exercises to validate BCP effectiveness. Conduct tabletop simulations, functional exercises, and full-scale drills to assess readiness.
  • Work closely with cross-functional teams, including IT, facilities, legal, and senior management, to ensure alignment and buy-in for business continuity efforts.
  • Provide training sessions to employees on BCPs, emergency procedures, and their roles during disruptions. Foster a culture of preparedness and awareness.
  • Regularly review and enhance business continuity strategies based on lessons learned, industry best practices, and changes in the business environment.

    Work Experience and Education:
  • Bachelor’s degree in Risk Management or Business with 6+ years of experience
  • 3+ years of supervisor or lead experience.
  • Insurance industry experience preferred

Licenses & Certifications:

Certified Business Continuity Professional (CBCP) or ISO 22301 Lead Implementer or Project Management Professional (PMP) is preferred

Technical/Functional Skills:

  • Risk assessment and risk management: Identifies, analyzes, and prioritizes operational, technology, third-party, and environmental risks, and develops practical risk mitigation strategies aligned with enterprise risk management frameworks.
  • Business impact analysis (BIA): Conducts BIAs to determine critical processes, dependencies, recovery time objectives (RTOs), recovery point objectives (RPOs), maximum tolerable downtime, and financial and operational impacts of disruption.
  • Business continuity and resilience planning: Develops and maintains business continuity plans, crisis management and emergency response plans, and recovery strategies in line with ISO 22301, DRI International, or Business Continuity Institute (BCI) standards and practices.
  • Strategic planning: Builds multi-year business continuity program roadmaps, defines program metrics, and aligns continuity priorities with business strategy and operational resilience goals.
  • IT disaster recovery and technology resilience: Partners with IT and information security to align application recovery priorities, system dependencies, and disaster recovery capabilities with business recovery requirements.
  • Third-party and vendor continuity: Evaluates the resilience of critical vendors, service providers, and delegated authority partners, including review of vendor continuity plans and recovery capabilities.
  • Business continuity software administration: Administers and configures business continuity planning platforms to manage plans, BIAs, contact data, assessments, and reporting.
  • Mass notification and threat intelligence administration: Manages emergency notification systems, including contact data quality, message templates, and delivery testing, and monitors threat intelligence sources to provide timely alerts on severe weather, safety, and other events affecting employees and operations.
  • Exercise design and facilitation: Designs, facilitates, and documents tabletop, functional, and full-scale exercises, and tracks resulting corrective actions through to completion.
  • Data analysis and reporting: Analyzes plan, exercise, and incident data to draw clear conclusions, and produces dashboards and metrics that inform decisions by leadership.
  • Presentation development and delivery: Develops and delivers clear, concise presentations and training materials to audiences ranging from front-line employees to senior executives.

Functional Requirements:

  • Own the enterprise business continuity program lifecycle, including governance, policy and standards, annual plan review and approval cycles, and program maintenance across all business units.
  • Lead and maintain the BIA process for all business units, and ensure results drive recovery strategies, resource requirements, and plan content.
  • Maintain business continuity, crisis management, and emergency response plans, and verify that plan owners review and update them at least annually and after significant organizational or operational change.
  • Plan and execute an annual schedule of exercises and tests, and document results, gaps, and corrective actions with assigned owners and due dates.
  • Coordinate the organization’s response during incidents and disruptions, including activating plans, convening the crisis management team, and supporting internal and external communications.
  • Conduct post-incident and post-exercise reviews, and incorporate lessons learned into plans, training, and program improvements.
  • Ensure the program meets applicable insurance regulatory, contractual, and audit requirements, such as state department of insurance expectations, NAIC guidance, and client or carrier due diligence requests.
  • Support client, carrier, regulator, and auditor inquiries by providing business continuity attestations, evidence, and documentation.
  • Report on program status, risks, exercise results, and key metrics to senior leadership, executive committees, and the board as required.
  • Manage the business continuity planning and mass notification platforms, including user access, data accuracy, and regular testing.
  • Develop and deliver business continuity awareness and training programs for employees, plan owners, and crisis management team members.
  • Supervise or lead business continuity staff, contractors, and a network of plan owners and coordinators, setting priorities and providing direction and coaching.

Behavioral Skills:

  • Effective communication: Communicates clearly and calmly in writing and verbally, tailoring messages for executives, technical teams, and employees, especially during high-pressure incidents.
  • Interpersonal skills and influence: Builds trusted relationships and gains buy-in across departments, business units, and levels of leadership without relying on direct authority.
  • Attention to detail: Maintains accurate, complete, and audit-ready plans, records, and contact data.
  • Decision making: Makes timely, well-informed decisions with incomplete information and balances risk, cost, and operational impact.
  • Problem-solving: Applies structured, analytical thinking to resolve complex issues and develop practical solutions.
  • Leadership and accountability: Leads by example, follows through on commitments, and holds teams and plan owners accountable for deliverables.
  • Continuous learning: Stays current on emerging threats, regulatory changes, and industry best practices, and applies new knowledge to improve the program.
  • Emotional intelligence: Remains composed under pressure, shows empathy toward affected employees, and adapts communication style to different audiences and situations

Our client is taking its own trading platform to mass market. You'll lead the Engagement tribe and report to the VP of Product, with two to three domain Product Managers reporting to you. You'll own the tribe's strategy, its key results and the development of its Product Managers.

  • Run the portfolio across trading and loyalty: sequence, trade off and stop what isn't working.

Qualifications and Experience

  • A B2C trading background. Candidates with a B2B product background will not be considered.

  • Has owned an engagement, retention or monetisation outcome with a number attached, on a CFD or multi-asset trading platform.
  • Real depth in the trading experience: order entry, risk controls, charting, signals, and how trader behaviour differs between a third-party terminal and a proprietary platform.
  • Has run retention mechanics and developed junior Product Managers.
  • Has raised a team's release and experiment cadence from a low base.
  • Commercial fluency in how engagement converts to value: ARPU, retention and what incentives cost.

jobs.description:
This is a remote position.

Remote (India) | Full-time

Also searched as: Notion Developer, Notion Consultant, Notion & Automation Specialist, No-Code Automation Specialist, Workspace Systems Specialist, Business Systems Specialist, AI Workflow Specialist, Knowledge Management Specialist

Could you design a Notion system so clear that a remote team runs its week from it, and then automate the parts nobody should be typing by hand?

On a typical day you might map with a team lead how requests move between people in the morning, wire a Notion database to Slack and HubSpot so status updates post themselves after lunch, and before you log off, run a short training for a team in Australia on the tracker you built for them.

About Contour

We operate across three brands. The India team, which falls under the Global Enablement and Support pillar, is the global capability centre (GCC) Contour is building: it runs delivery, automation, people, and operations for the whole organisation.

The Kind of People Who Thrive Here

Contour started in 2020 as one classroom in a university library. In 2022 three full-time team members ran the business on Monday.com. Today we are about 600 people across Australia and India, and much of what we run was built by someone who noticed it was missing.

The work matters. More than 10,000 students rely on what we build, from the booklets they study from to the systems their families pay through. The people who do well here care about that and want to know their work made a difference to those students.

They own their work end to end, start things without being asked, and finish what they commit to. They tell the truth early, including when something is off and what they have already tried, and write decisions down so the next person can pick them up. They give direct feedback and ask for it back.

The pace is fast. Small problems are fixed the same week, bigger ones within the six-week cycle, and whoever spots the problem usually gets to lead the fix. We keep refining how we work, and you are expected to improve the processes you own.

We hire on what you have built and run yourself, and growth works the same way. Time with us counts, but scope, title and pay move with what you deliver and how much you raise the bar on what you own.

The GCC is being built now, seat by seat. This one decides whether the way teams track their work holds up as Contour grows.

About This Role

You are Contour's Notion builder. You design the databases, workflows and automations that teams plan and track their work in, connect them to the other tools Contour runs on, then document them and run the training until the new setup sticks.

Teams in India and Australia already keep trackers in Notion, but use is uneven, and much of it was set up by whoever needed it first. You sit in Business Operations and build for every team in the GCC: Operations and project coordinators, Customer Support, Academics and content, People and Finance, as well as the Australian teams they work with. The Internal Product team is your partner for anything that needs code. Teams tell you what they need to see; the build, the guides and the rollout are yours.

This is international work. Many of the people who rely on your systems sit in Melbourne, so you run trainings, answer questions and take feedback across the India–Australia time difference, in clear written and spoken English.

Two things separate a strong hire from a competent one here. First, you build for the person using it: someone new can find and change their tasks without a walkthrough, and a structure that only makes sense once you explain it is unfinished. Second, when a team copies data between tools or chases updates by hand, your first move is to automate it, with Notion's own automations, Notion AI, or Make, Zapier or n8n, and you measure what it saved.

This is an individual contributor seat: you manage nobody and work alongside the teams that rely on Notion. A build counts as finished once people use it, and a tracker nobody fills in is your problem to solve. Contour is scaling and hires for the long term: the scope of this seat grows with the platform, and what you deliver decides how fast.

When a workspace is clear, a lead sees what is open without calling a meeting, and a joiner learns how a team operates by reading it.

What You Will Do

  • Map the process before designing:Sit with each team to list what they track, who updates it and what each person checks, then settle the structure.

  • Design the databases:Link them with relations, rollups and formulas so each fact is entered once and appears wherever it is needed.

  • Set up views for every role:Give the requester, the person doing the task and the lead their own view, filtered to what they act on.

  • Automate the repetitive steps:Replace copying, chasing and hand-typed status updates with Notion buttons, database automations and templates.

  • Connect Notion to the rest of the stack:Use Make, Zapier, n8n or the Notion API to link HubSpot, Slack, Google Workspace and Monday, so work moves between tools without anyone retyping it.

  • Put AI to work:Set up Notion AI and AI agents to summarise requests, draft SOPs, answer "how do I" questions from the workspace, and keep pages tidy, with a person checking what matters.

  • Write the guides:Document each setup in plain words: what it is for, how to add to it, and what to update when.

  • Run each rollout:Train teams in India and Australia in short live sessions and one to one, answer questions through the first weeks, and adjust what you made from what you hear.

  • Keep the workspace in order:Look after permissions, naming and archiving, and retire pages no one visits.

If a better tool exists for something we are doing manually, make the case and we will back it.


Requirements

What You Need

We weigh what you have built and run more than the years on your CV. You should be able to point to:

  • A Notion workspace you designed and built for a team at work, which they ran their day from. Personal templates and course projects don't count here.

  • Automation and AI (essential):a manual step you removed with an automation, an integration or an AI step, using Notion automations, Make, Zapier, n8n or similar, and the time or errors it saved.

  • A guide you wrote or a training you ran after which people used a system without coming back to you.

  • A messy or abandoned setup you inherited and rebuilt, with the old records moved across intact.

  • International exposure (essential):systems you built, trained or supported for colleagues or clients in another country, ideally Australia, the UK or the US.

  • Excellent written and spoken English that a colleague in Australia follows first time, in a doc, on Slack or in a live training.

You know relations, rollups, formulas, templates and permissions well enough to see where a structure will break before anyone relies on it.

If you have delivered these, or can show us how you would here, apply. If you enjoy hands-on building, this seat will suit you; if your recent years have mostly been signing off other people's work, it may feel small.

Nice to Have

  • Knowledge management:a team wiki, SOP library or onboarding hub you built or ran, which people used and kept current.

  • Project management and coordination:cross-team work you ran or coordinated, with timelines, owners and status that stakeholders could rely on.

  • Scrum Master or agile delivery:sprints, stand-ups and retros you ran, with clean boards and data and clear progress updates for leads.

  • Notion API, webhooks or light scripting (JavaScript, Python or Apps Script).

  • HubSpot, Monday or Google Workspace administration.

  • Building custom GPTs or AI agents for a team.

  • An education or student-facing background.

What Good Looks Like

  • In daily use:the teams you set up keep their records current without anyone chasing them.

  • Easy to find:anyone can reach the current version of a page in one search.

  • Less manual work:the top repeat hand-offs between tools run on their own, and you can show the hours saved.

  • AI in the workflow:teams use Notion AI and the agents you set up every week, and trust what they produce.


Benefits

Fully remote, anywhere in India, and comfortable working across the India and Australia time difference. Compensation is competitive and benchmarked to the role and your experience; we discuss it openly early in the process.

Ready to build the Notion systems Contour's teams run on, and automate what slows them down? Apply now.

jobs.title: Technical Project Lead (all genders)
jobs.excerpt: über das arbeiten bei envelio Zu einfach ist langweilig!
jobs.description:
über das arbeiten bei envelio

Zu einfach ist langweilig! Gemeinsam haben wir die Mission, die Energiewende voranzutreiben. Wir lieben, was wir tun und dabei ist uns kein Thema zu groß. Wir übernehmen Verantwortung für unsere Arbeit und wachsen an jeder neuen Aufgabe. Kurz gesagt: Own it, love it, grow with it.

Wir sind ein bodenständiges Team aus Kaffee- und Mate-Liebhaber:innen. Unser Geek-Humor resultiert in einer rituellen Nutzung von Emojis und der enzyklopädischen Herausarbeitung von unnützem Wissen. Mehr als 250 envelianer:innen mit über 20 verschiedenen Nationalitäten sind bereits an Bord. Komm dazu und wachse mit uns!

deine rolle

Als Technical Project Lead (all genders) führst du technisch komplexe Kunden- und Entwicklungsprojekte und bist dafür verantwortlich, dass envelio verbindliche Lieferzusagen termingerecht und abnahmesicher erfüllt. Du planst technische Umsetzungen, entscheidest über Produktoptionen, löst Konflikte und verhandelst, intern über alle beteiligten Entwicklungsteams hinweg ebenso wie gegenüber dem Kunden.

Dabei gilt eine klare Aufgabenteilung: Das Produktmanagement verantwortet Produktstrategie, Kundenproblem und angestrebte Ergebnisse, Engineering die technische Lösung bis zum Release. Du verantwortest das Lieferergebnis deiner Projekte: Scope, Termin und Abnahme. Innerhalb des vereinbarten Projektrahmens triffst du die dafür nötigen Entscheidungen, auch wenn sich die Beteiligten (intern wie extern) nicht einig sind.

Typische Einsatzfelder sind Projekte, die mehrere Entwicklungsteams betreffen, parallele technische Tracks mit relevanten Abhängigkeiten haben, einen neuen Markt oder Use Case erschließen oder an engen, umsatzrelevanten Abnahmemeilensteinen hängen. Beispiele sind Ausschreibungen, Projekte mit Enterprisekunden und vertraglich vereinbarte Entwicklungsprojekte, zunehmend auch mit internationalen Kunden - z.B. bei unserer Tochterfirma in Nordamerika.

Du arbeitest eng mit Projekt- und Programmleitung, Produktmanagement, Tech Leads und Engineering sowie mit Sales, Customer Success und Management zusammen. Die Rolle ist eine Führungsrolle in der Sache, ohne disziplinarische Personalverantwortung.

wie du etwas bewirkst

Projekt führen

  • Ab der Übergabe aus Sales und Pre-Sales entwickelst du mit Projektleitung, Produktmanagement und Engineering den Lieferplan: Scope, Meilensteine, Abhängigkeiten, Risiken und überprüfbare Abnahmekriterien. Delivery-Risiken adressierst du, bevor sie zum Problem werden.
  • Du triffst die für die Lieferung nötigen Entscheidungen, z. B. zu Scope-Schnitt, Priorisierung und Reihenfolge innerhalb des Projekts, auch in festgefahrenen Situationen. Eskaliert werden nur Fragen, die das angestrebte Produktergebnis oder eine Vertragszusage verändern, und dann mit einer klaren Empfehlung.
  • Konkurrierende Prioritäten, Kapazitätsengpässe und Zielkonflikte zwischen Teams löst du in der Regel aktiv auf und eskalierst sie in Ausnahmesituation an das Leadership Team.
  • Du etablierst eine dem Projektrisiko angemessene Steuerung (z. B. Kickoff, Steerings, Risiko-Reviews), berichtest adressatengerecht bis zum Steering Board und führst das Projekt durch Abnahme und Übergabe in den Regelbetrieb.
Technisch steuern
  • Du arbeitest dich tief in die Architektur unserer Plattform ein und weißt, welches Team wofür zuständig ist. So bringst du Themen direkt zu den richtigen Teams.
  • Du begleitest Anforderungen nicht nur im Prozess, sondern auch inhaltlich, und machst konkrete Vorschläge, wie sich der Scope schneiden lässt, ohne das angestrebte Ergebnis zu gefährden und gleichzeitig die Strategie des Produktmanagements zu verfolgen.
  • Du hinterfragst Aufwandsschätzungen und Lösungsansätze kritisch und diskutierst Alternativen auf Architekturebene mit Lead Engineers.
Kunde & Verhandlung
  • Du bist für den Kunden der technische Ansprechpartner zu Lieferumfang, Meilensteinen, Abhängigkeiten von Kundenzuarbeiten und Abnahme. Wo es keine andere kundenseitige Projektleitung gibt, insbesondere in vertraglich vereinbarten Entwicklungsprojekten, führst du das Projekt auch nach außen.
  • Du verhandelst Scope-Änderungen, Deadlines und Abnahmekriterien mit Kunden ebenso wie intern mit Produktmanagement und Engineering und erzielst tragfähige Ergebnisse.
  • Wo eine Projekt- oder Programmleitung benannt ist, verantwortet sie den kommerziellen Erfolg und die Kundenbeziehung, du die technische Lieferung. Wesentliche Änderungen stimmt ihr vor der Kommunikation an den Kunden ab.

dein profil

Perfektion ist ein Mythos! Vielmehr interessiert uns der Mensch hinter dem Bildschirm. Diese Kriterien sind also eher als Orientierungshilfe für dich gedacht. Wir sind gespannt, wie deine individuellen Fähigkeiten zu uns passen.

  • Mehrjährige Erfahrung in der Verantwortung für die Lieferung komplexer Softwareprojekte, z. B. als Technical Project oder Program Lead, gerne mit Hintergrund als Software Engineer, Architekt:in oder technische:r Consultant; Erfahrung mit Kundenprojekten mit vertraglichen Deadlines und Abnahmen, idealerweise aus Ausschreibungen oder Enterprise-Projekten.
  • Du verstehst Softwarearchitekturen, Systemintegration sowie Test-, Release- und Abnahmeprozesse so gut, dass du Aufwandsschätzungen plausibilisieren und mit Lead Engineers auf Augenhöhe über Lösungsalternativen diskutieren kannst. Moderne, auch AI-gestützte Entwicklungspraktiken sind dir vertraut.
  • Du übernimmst Ergebnisverantwortung, triffst Entscheidungen auch unter Unsicherheit und führst ohne Weisungsbefugnis über Klarheit, Kompetenz und Durchsetzungsvermögen.
  • Du verhandelst souverän mit Kunden, Produktmanagement und Engineering und findest Lösungen, die Ergebnis und Termin zugleich sichern.
  • Du steuerst so viel wie nötig und mit so wenig Overhead wie möglich.
  • Du kommunizierst komplexe Sachverhalte klar und prägnant, gegenüber Product Management und Engineering ebenso wie gegenüber Kunden, Partnern und Management.
  • Ein Verständnis der Energiebranche, der Verteilnetzbetreiber und ihres regulatorischen Umfelds ist von Vorteil.
  • Sehr gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift.

deine benefits

  • Passe den Arbeitsmodus an deinen Lifestyle an – fully remote oder hybrid mit Office-Option
  • Option zum mobilen Arbeiten aus dem Ausland (bis zu 90 Tage pro Jahr von überall in der EU oder den USA)
  • 30 Urlaubstage + 3 corporate holidays
  • Unterstützung deiner Gesundheit mit der Urban Sports Club Kooperation
  • Flexible Nutzung eines monatlichen Mobilitätsbudgets (z.B. Jobrad, ÖPNV)
  • Zeit und Budget für individuelles Wachstum
  • optionale betriebliche Altersvorsorge
  • Professionelle Unterstützung für dein psychisches Wohlbefinden durch unseren Partner nilo – für dich und deine Familie
  • Regelmäßige Tech und Growth Talks zum internen Wissensaustausch
  • Regelmäßige Company und Team Events
  • Sehr gute Hardware-Ausstattung (16 Zoll MacBooks, 2 Bildschirme in unserem Büro in Köln)

jobs.title: Data Scientist
jobs.excerpt: About Us: Zest Health is redefining care for the 40M+ Americans with chronic dermatologic conditions like eczema and psoriasis.
jobs.description:
About Us:

Zest Health is redefining care for the 40M+ Americans with chronic dermatologic conditions like eczema and psoriasis. Through our virtual dermatology clinic, Zest is making care more accessible, effective, and affordable. Join our well-resourced, passionate team as we set the new gold standard for value-based specialty care.

Job Summary

We are looking for a Data Scientist with experience in healthcare, finance, or insurance, specifically pharmacy benefits and pharmacy claims. You will use pharmacy claims data to measure the clinical and financial impact of our programs and present findings to health plan, PBM, and clinical audiences. The Data Scientist supports our Chief Growth Officer by translating pharmacy claims into savings analyses and clinical evidence for health plan and PBM partners and prospects. The role also supports our operations and clinical teams in defining and validating the methodology behind partner reporting.

Scope of Work

  • Analyze pharmacy claims to evaluate adherence, persistence, utilization, and cost outcomes
  • Translate partner questions about medication utilization and spend into documented analyses of financial impact
  • Define and validate comparison groups, adherence measures, and outcome measures, assess confounding, and characterize uncertainty
  • Analyze biosimilar adoption, dose optimization, and formulary alignment
  • Build models and scenario analyses that quantify savings and ROI, and test the assumptions behind them
  • Support quarterly business reviews and partner evidence requests with clear written analyses
  • Present findings to technical and non-technical stakeholders, including health plan, PBM, and clinical teams
  • Partner with clinical, finance, and data teams to define metrics and validate methods
  • Follow privacy and data governance requirements for protected health information

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in a quantitative field, or equivalent specialized training or experience
  • Experience in healthcare, finance, or insurance, specifically pharmacy benefits and pharmacy claims
  • 4+ years of experience analyzing pharmacy claims, dispensing data, and medication utilization or adherence measures
  • 4+ years of experience with SQL and Python or R to query, manipulate, and analyze data
  • Working knowledge of drug identifiers and classifications such as NDC, GPI, generic and brand, and therapeutic class, and of pharmacy claim formats such as NCPDP
  • Experience calculating adherence and persistence measures, including proportion of days covered (PDC) and medication possession ratio (MPR)
  • Working knowledge of rebates, formulary operations, and net-cost concepts, including estimating net cost from gross claims using stated rebate assumptions, and of biosimilar strategies
  • 4+ years of experience building statistical and financial models and applying analytic methods beyond descriptive analysis, including comparison groups
  • 2+ years of experience presenting technical and clinical findings to non-technical stakeholders

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master's degree or advanced training in biostatistics, epidemiology, pharmacoepidemiology, health services research, public health, pharmacy, data science, or statistics
  • Experience with PBM data and claims adjudication
  • Experience with value-based contracts and ROI guarantees
  • Experience at an early-stage company

Equal Employment Opportunity

Zest Health is committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all applicants and employees in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local laws. Employment decisions are made without regard to any characteristic protected by applicable law.

We care more about what you've built than a perfect resume match. If you've designed pharmacy models that held up under scrutiny, you learn fast, and build before the need exists, we want to hear from you even if you don't check every box.

About Kinaxis

Are you looking to join an innovative, market-leading company where you can truly elevate your career? If you are looking to be part of an incredible growth story, then we might just be the place for you!

In 1984, we started out as a team of three engineers. Today, we have grown to become a global organization with over 2000 employees around the world, 6 global office and a best-in-class HQ in Ottawa, Canada. As winners of several Top Employer awards globally, we are proud to work with our customers and employees towards solving some of the biggest challenges facing supply chains today.

Kinaxis is a global leader in modern supply chain orchestration, powering complex global supply chains, and supporting the people who manage them. Our powerful, AI infused platform provides full transparency and visibility across end-to-end supply chains, enabling our customers to make faster, better decisions. We are trusted by renowned global brands to provide the agility and predictability needed to navigate today’s volatility and disruption. With more than 40,000 users in over 100 countries, we are expanding our team as we continue to innovate and revolutionize how we support our customers.

#Senior

Become a part of our caring community

Manager, Project Management

Lead complex initiatives. Develop great teams. Help expand how children and families access care.

At Nemours Children’s Health, project management is about more than delivering projects on time. It is about bringing strategy, people, technology, clinical operations, and resources together to advance our mission and create healthier futures for children.

We are seeking an experienced Manager, Project Management to join our Strategic Project Management team and lead complex, system-wide initiatives across our multi-state health system.

As Manager, Project Management, you'll provide day-to-day leadership for approximately 6–8 associates, with a primary focus on Ambulatory Market Expansion projects. You'll coordinate workload, coach and develop project management talent, support project sponsors, implement PMO standards, and help teams navigate complex delivery challenges.

For issues requiring broader organizational decisions, you'll serve as a critical connection between project teams, sponsors, and senior leadership.

What You'll Do

Lead a Complex Project Portfolio

  • Oversee delivery of a portfolio of complex, cross-functional initiatives.
  • Ensure portfolio outcomes remain aligned with enterprise strategy.
  • Monitor project schedules, budgets, risks, dependencies, resources, and outcomes.
  • Use quantitative analysis and project data to evaluate portfolio health and identify areas requiring intervention.
  • Drive portfolio prioritization, sequencing, governance, and executive reporting.
  • Support Ambulatory Market Expansion and other strategic initiatives across a complex, multi-state healthcare environment.

Develop & Lead a High-Performing Team

  • Provide day-to-day leadership, workload coordination, and coaching for approximately 6–8 associates.
  • Develop project managers and coordinators while building capabilities for increasingly complex work.
  • Support performance management, career development, and succession planning.
  • Align team capacity and capabilities with portfolio priorities.
  • Foster accountability, collaboration, continuous improvement, and delivery excellence.

Partner with Sponsors & Executive Leaders

  • Build trusted relationships with senior and executive stakeholders, including VP, CFO, and CNO-level leaders.
  • Provide guidance and support to project sponsors throughout the project lifecycle.
  • Serve as an escalation point for complex delivery challenges.
  • Elevate issues requiring senior leadership decisions and provide the data and context needed to support informed decision-making.
  • Drive alignment across clinical, operational, technical, and facilities stakeholders.

What You'll Bring

Required

  • Bachelor's degree.
  • 8+ years of project/program management experience.
  • PMP or equivalent certification.
  • Strong project and portfolio management experience.
  • Advanced risk, dependency, and prioritization capabilities.
  • Strong analytical, data management, and problem-solving skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead complex, cross-functional initiatives.
  • Strong executive communication, influence, and stakeholder-management skills.

Preferred

  • Master's degree.
  • Previous people leadership experience.
  • Experience with Epic, Oracle, and/or mergers and acquisitions.

Why This Role Matters

This is an opportunity to step into a leadership role with genuine enterprise impact.

With 60–80 active projects, roughly 25 new requests arriving each month, and initiatives touching virtually every aspect of our health system, you'll help determine not only how work gets delivered, but how priorities are translated into meaningful outcomes.

Your immediate leadership will be particularly important as Nemours advances Ambulatory Market Expansion initiatives, requiring disciplined project execution, strong sponsor relationships, thoughtful resource coordination, and the ability to navigate dependencies across multiple functions and locations.

Our mission goes well beyond medicine. We're working to create the healthiest generations of children by bringing together clinical care, research, education, advocacy, prevention, and meaningful partnerships with the communities we serve.

jobs.description:
Smart Tech Contracting delivers turnkey BAS & EPMS solutions for mission-critical colocation and hyperscale data centers operating at national program scale. As a Master Systems Integrator (MSI), we unify controls construction (DDC, PLC, SCADA) with software engineering, optimized graphics / UI standards, and program-level governance.

Complex integrations are delivered cleanly, consistently, and fast. Our teams thrive in high-stakes environments where quality control and uptime matters, schedules are compressed, and coordination is everything.

Join us and be part of a team where your voice matters, your work makes an impact, and your growth is a shared priority.

Position Title: Information Security Manager

Position Location: Remote - work virtually from anywhere in the United States - Dallas, TX OR Austin, TX preferred

JOB SUMMARY

The Information Security Manager leads Smart Tech Contracting’s information security program as the company scales from a small specialty contractor into a midsize, technology-driven organization. The role spans every STC technology function, including cloud and infrastructure, software development, AI and data services, and field operations, and represents STC’s security posture to clients, auditors, and partner organizations. STC is growing rapidly across a fully remote national workforce, and there is no internal security team today; this role builds the program and the team that runs it.

STC software developers, field engineers, and field technicians program controllers on client sites, connect to client networks, and build software and AI-enabled tools for internal use and for clients. The Information Security Manager is an enabler of that work, not a gatekeeper. Success is measured by how much faster staff can move safely: routine access approved in minutes or hours, admin rights granted through secure self-service rather than a ticket queue, new tools reviewed in days rather than weeks, and client security questionnaires answered accurately with evidence behind every answer. Policies are co-created with the teams who follow them, so the secure path is also the easiest path.

This role bridges technical security operations and business-level governance. The Information Security Manager operates with substantial autonomy and runs the security program day to day, stays hands-on with the Microsoft security stack, measures whether controls actually work, and builds the security team as STC grows.

This role is NOT responsible for AI strategy or AI tool selection. Special Projects & Innovation (SPI) and the AI Program Manager own AI tool decisions; this role reviews the security and data handling of tools SPI has vetted, quickly and with clear conditions. This role is also not the administrator of STC’s cloud platforms: the Cloud Architecture Manager builds and operates Azure, Microsoft 365, and Entra ID, while the Information Security Manager sets their security requirements and verifies the controls work. Security design of the control systems STC delivers to clients sits with STC’s engineering departments; this role defines how STC staff and devices connect to client operational technology.

The Information Security Manager reports to the IT Director and works closely with the Cloud Architecture Manager, STC’s software development teams, SPI and the AI Program Manager, department and field leaders, and STC’s managed service provider (MSP) and security partners.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

Security Program Leadership and Strategy (15%)

  • Define and execute STC’s information security strategy and roadmap in alignment with business objectives, the annual IT plan, and leadership’s risk tolerance.
  • Build, lead, and develop the security team across governance, risk, compliance, identity, and technical security disciplines, within the IT headcount plan.
  • Establish and chair the Information Security Committee, setting the agenda, driving decisions, and ensuring cross-functional alignment.
  • Manage security vendor relationships, including managed detection and response (MDR), vulnerability management, and tooling partners, and own the security program budget within the IT budget.
  • Report on security posture, risk, control effectiveness, and program maturity to the IT Director and senior leadership on a regular cadence.

Field and Builder Enablement (20%)

  • Work proactively with software developers, field engineers, field technicians, SPI, and department leaders to understand how they work and co-create policies that are secure and let them move faster.
  • Replace waits for admin access with secure self-service options, including just-in-time or time-limited elevation, pre-approved software catalogs, and approved settings staff can apply themselves.
  • Establish field-ready device and endpoint standards that support controls work on client sites, including engineering and programming software, controller connections, and access to client networks.
  • Define the security controls for how STC staff, devices, and remote connections reach client operational technology, aligned with ISA / IEC 62443, without disrupting field work.
  • Define tiered review paths and time-boxed exceptions so routine requests are approved in minutes or hours and higher-risk requests in days; track wait times and continuously remove blockers.

Governance, Risk, and Compliance (25%)

  • Maintain STC’s security policies and standards within the IT policy framework the IT Director owns, aligned to NIST CSF, ISO 27001, SOC 2, and CIS Benchmarks, and present them to the Information Security Committee for review and approval.
  • Lead SOC 2 readiness and attestation, including scope, control mapping, evidence collection, and auditor engagement.
  • Maintain and mature the security risk register, conducting periodic risk assessments and ensuring risk acceptance decisions are documented and reviewed.
  • Serve as the primary point of contact for client security questionnaires, external audits, and compliance reviews, giving accurate, evidence-backed answers.
  • Conduct third-party security assessments of vendors and partners.
  • Ensure AI and data initiatives meet STC’s data protection requirements, applying the AI data-governance guardrails the IT Director sets in partnership with SPI.

Security Architecture and Technical Oversight (15%)

  • Set security baselines for Microsoft 365, Azure, and related cloud services, and verify that the controls the Cloud Architecture Manager and partners implement work as intended.
  • Define identity security requirements, including Conditional Access, Privileged Identity Management, service-principal standards, and access reviews.
  • Guide the design of data protection controls, including data loss prevention, information protection labeling, and insider risk management.
  • Run the vulnerability management program and build application security checks into the CI/CD pipelines and templates teams already use.
  • Evaluate and approve emerging security capabilities, ensuring alignment with STC’s risk posture and technology roadmap.

Security Operations and Incident Response (15%)

  • Oversee security operations, including MDR integration, SIEM and SOAR management, and alert tuning.
  • Own the security incident response program, including documented plans, escalation procedures, tabletop exercises, and post-incident reviews.
  • Lead response to security events, coordinating internal teams, external partners, and client security teams, and escalating major incidents to the IT Director.
  • Drive continuous improvement of detection and response through lessons learned and threat intelligence.
  • Security Awareness and Stakeholder Engagement (10%)
  • Deliver a security awareness program for all STC personnel, including role-specific guidance and periodic phishing simulations measured for effectiveness.
  • Represent STC’s security posture with clients, strategic partners, and steering committees, including security scorecard reviews and posture assessments.
  • Use automation and AI inside the security program itself, such as automated evidence collection, alert triage, and questionnaire responses.

Completion of Assigned Tasks and Deliverables on Time and on Budget

Performs Other Related Duties as Assigned

POSITION REQUIREMENTS (ADVANCED LEVEL FOR ALL THE FOLLOWING)

  • Expert knowledge of Microsoft Entra ID identity governance, RBAC, Conditional Access, Privileged Identity Management, and external identities (B2B and Entra External ID).
  • Strong knowledge of the Microsoft Defender suite (Endpoint, Identity, Office 365, and Cloud Apps) and Microsoft Purview Information Protection.
  • Strong knowledge of securing Microsoft 365 workloads, including Exchange Online, SharePoint, Teams, and Power Platform.
  • Strong knowledge of endpoint privilege management (just-in-time elevation, LAPS, and Intune) that gives users the access they need without standing admin rights.
  • Strong knowledge of security frameworks and compliance programs, including SOC 2, ISO 27001, NIST CSF, CIS Benchmarks, security questionnaires, and audit evidence.
  • Strong knowledge of vulnerability management, endpoint security, and network security principles.
  • Knowledge of SIEM and SOAR platforms (Microsoft Sentinel preferred) and incident response workflows.
  • Knowledge of Azure services (App Service, Key Vault, Storage, Virtual Network, and Private Link) and infrastructure-as-code patterns.
  • Knowledge of application security, secure development lifecycle (SDLC) practices, and CI/CD pipeline security.
  • Knowledge of IT / OT security principles, including ISA / IEC 62443, as they apply to staff and devices connecting to client control systems.
  • Skilled in building, leading, and developing a security team in a remote environment.
  • Skilled in co-creating security policies, standards, and procedures with business, engineering, or field teams so they improve both security and speed.
  • Skilled in managing vendor relationships, contracts, and third-party security assessments.
  • Skilled in translating security risk into concise business language for executives, non-technical leaders, and field staff.
  • Skilled at using MS Office Suite (Excel, Word, Outlook, PowerPoint, Teams), along with exceptional organizational skills for file management.
  • Ability to work hands-on in the Microsoft security stack while leading the security program.
  • Ability to balance speed and control, and to say yes safely when staff want to try something new.
  • Ability to communicate effectively in both oral and written form with executives, auditors, clients, and field personnel.
  • Ability to work successfully in a remote environment, as a collaborative leader and independently with minimal supervision.
  • Ability to follow company and site safety requirements.
  • Ability to work under pressure and meet close deadlines.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

The following physical demands must be met by the employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is:

  • Frequently required to remain in a stationary position and operate a computer
  • Occasionally moving through office, client, and critical facility environments, including data centers and active construction sites
  • Occasionally ascending and descending stairs to access equipment rooms
  • On occasion the employee may move equipment weighing up to 25 pounds

TRAVEL / RELOCATION REQUIREMENTS

  • Up to 10%, this may include travel to any or all 50 US states
  • Effective May 7, 2025, and in accordance with U.S. federal regulations for domestic air travel, a valid REAL ID (or an acceptable alternative, such as a passport) is required for travel associated with this position.
  • Travel may involve transportation by car or plane depending on the destination and nature of the business need.
  • Travel is defined as physically leaving home on behalf of business activities including but not limited to client sites, meetings with other employees, vendor and partner meetings, meetings for business development purposes, running errands on behalf of the business, attending industry conferences, etc.

EDUCATION / EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS

  • Bachelor’s degree in information technology, information systems, computer science, cybersecurity, or related discipline

OR

  • Four additional years of hands-on information security or IT experience

PLUS

  • Minimum five years of progressive information security experience, including at least two years in a security leadership, program management, or governance role
  • CISSP (Certified Information Systems Security Professional) or CISM (Certified Information Security Manager) certification
  • Must have built or run a security program, including verifying that controls work, not only writing policy
  • Must have led SOC 2 readiness or a similar compliance program hands-on
  • Must have hands-on experience with the Microsoft security stack, including Intune and endpoint privilege management
  • Must have co-created security policy with business, engineering, or field teams
  • Experience reducing admin-access friction through just-in-time elevation or self-service, or supporting field, construction, OT, or industrial workforces, is strongly preferred
  • Experience enabling software developers or AI builders, or serving as the first security hire at a growing company, is preferred

BENEFITS

Smart Tech Contracting offers a very competitive benefits package; highlights include

  • Choice of comprehensive medical plans (including two PPO-style plans and a HDHP w/ HSA option)
  • Dental and vision plans
  • Comprehensive medical, dental and vision benefits extended to spouse / domestic partner and dependent children up to age 26
  • 401k with company match and self-directed brokerage account option
  • PTO including additional paid time off during the last week of the year
  • Company paid life insurance coverage for employees and their eligible dependents
  • Short and long-term disability, AD&D coverage
  • Professional development opportunities, tuition reimbursement and professional licensing assistance
  • Paid parental leave after one year of employment

CO, CA, IL, NY, WA, and Washington DC residents only: In accordance with CO, CA, IL, NY, WA, and Washington DC law, the range provided is STC's reasonable estimate of the base compensation for this role. The actual amount may differ based on non-discriminatory factors such as experience, knowledge, skills, abilities, and location.

Smart Tech Contracting is an EEO/Affirmative Action Employer and participates in the E-Verify program with the Department of Homeland Security. We encourage diversity in our workforce.

We envision a world in which all people have access to high-quality and enduring solutions to improve and maintain their health and well-being.

Our mission is to improve the health and well-being of people worldwide through enduring, high-quality, cost-effective, and universally accessible public health solutions. MCD operates impactful programs both in the United States and internationally.

Position Summary

MCD Global Health is seeking an experienced Senior Manager, Corporate Accounting to oversee the organization's day-to-day accounting operations and full accounting cycle. Reporting directly to the Chief Financial Officer (CFO), this position plays a critical role in ensuring the accuracy, integrity, and timeliness of financial information while supporting the development of efficient, modern financial processes.

The Senior Manager will lead key accounting functions, including monthly and year-end close, general ledger management, accounts payable and receivable, payroll accounting, cash management, indirect cost tracking, and revenue recognition. The position will work closely with the CFO and collaborate with the Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A) and reporting team to support sound financial management and organizational accountability.

This role also provides direct supervision to the Associate Manager of Corporate Finance and Accounting and the Manager of Payroll, fostering a collaborative, accountable, and supportive team environment.

Salary offers may be higher or lower than the anticipated salary range based on various factors, including the selected candidate's qualifications, experience, and geographic location within or outside of Maine.

Essential Job Functions:

1. General Ledger and Fund Accounting

Own the general ledger, chart of accounts, and fund and project coding so data stays accurate across all funding sources. Track net assets with and without donor restrictions in accordance with FASB ASC 958.

2. Monthly and Year-End Close

Lead the monthly and year-end close on a set calendar, including accruals, prepaids, fixed assets, account reconciliations, journal entries, and GAAP-compliant financial statements. Deliver closed, reconciled data to the FP&A and reporting team by agreed deadlines each month.

3. Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, and Payroll Accounting

Oversee AP, AR, and collections. Oversee payroll accounting, including fringe and benefit allocations and payroll tax filings.

4. Cash Management

Manage bank reconciliations, payment runs, bank account administration, and short-term cash forecasting.

5. Revenue Recognition

Own revenue recognition for grants, cooperative agreements, and cost-reimbursable government contracts in accordance with ASC 958-605 and ASC 606.

6. Indirect Cost Tracking and NICRA Support

Track indirect costs and monitor provisional versus actual rates. Support the annual Negotiated Indirect Cost Rate Agreement (NICRA) proposal and true-ups in compliance with 2 CFR 200 and FAR cost principles.

7. Internal Controls, Policies, and Compliance

Maintain internal controls, segregation of duties, and the accounting policies and procedures manual. Manage tax and regulatory compliance, including Form 990 support, 1099s, and state registrations.

8. Audit Coordination

Serve as main contact for the annual financial statement audit and Single Audit. Prepare audit schedules and supporting documentation, and resolve findings.

9. Finance Transformation

Partner with the CFO to redesign workflows, strengthen controls, and introduce automation and new systems that support lean, effective finance operations.

10. Team Leadership

Lead and develop the Associate Manager of Corporate Finance and Accounting and the Manager of Payroll. Set clear deadlines and performance measures, provide coaching and feedback, and build a supportive team culture.

Requirements

Senior Manager, Corporate Accounting

  • Grade Level: 7

  • Anticipated Salary: $120,000–$140,000

  • Reporting Relationship: Chief Financial Officer (CFO)

  • Bachelor’s degree in accounting required.

  • Certified Public Accountant (CPA) preferred. Candidates with a CPA in progress are encouraged to apply.

  • Minimum of eight (8) years of progressive accounting experience, including at least three (3) years managing staff.

  • Public accounting or audit firm experience.

  • Strong technical accounting skills, with deep knowledge of payroll accounting and revenue recognition for nonprofits and government contractors.

  • Working knowledge of GAAP, ASC 958, 2 CFR 200, and FAR cost principles. NICRA experience is a plus.

  • Strong reconciliation skills and a proven ability to identify issues and find solutions.

  • Highly organized and disciplined approach to deadlines, controls, and documentation.

  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel.

  • Experience with Blackbaud Financial Edge NXT or other ERP systems preferred.

  • Experience implementing or transitioning payroll or ERP systems is a strong plus.

  • Demonstrated record of process improvement and a strong commitment to continuous learning and new skills.

  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and exercise sound judgment.

Job Description

Work at Home Bilingual Tzotzil-English Phone Interpreter


Job Title: Tzotzil Interpreter

Location: Work at Home position in United States

Position: Phone Interpreter

Status: Independent Contractor

Pay: $1.30 - $1.45 per minute
